papers.title: Ohmic warm inflation
papers.summary: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.

papers.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
papers.summary: It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($δ$) is 0 or $π$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$, but not the $ν_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sinδ$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile. For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sinδ$ dependence to be probed in $ν_μ$ survival probability. We also discuss future experimental scenarios that could probe T/CP-violation in $ν_μ$ survival probability.

papers.title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II
papers.summary: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^α\cap L_t^2H_x^{α+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leqα<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty. \] Thus non-uniqueness holds in optimal Sobolev spaces and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin weak spaces, even in a symmetry class where smooth solutions are globally regular. The proof relies on a computer-assisted construction of a linearly unstable forward self-similar solution, starting from the numerical profiles identified in our preceding paper (arXiv:2606.07501). We combine explicit asymptotic expansions and global residual estimates with weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals. Approximate solutions of auxiliary linear equations yield quantitative inverse bounds, allowing us to correct both the stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair by contraction arguments. The instability and localization theorem proved in arXiv:2606.07501 then produces the non-unique solutions.

papers.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
papers.summary: We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $α$-moment $ν$ for some unknown $α\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on the covariates, any finite-variance subroutine attaining the sub-Gaussian rate yields the following when the number of samples $n$ is above a suitably defined threshold: Without knowing $α$ or $ν$, we have with probability at least $1-δ$ that $ \|\widehatθ-θ^*\|_Σ \lesssim_α ν^{1/α} \big(\frac{d+\log(1/δ)}{n}\big)^{\frac{α-1}α}, $ where $d$ is the dimension, $Σ$ is the covariate covariance matrix, and $\|v\|_Σ:=(v^\topΣv)^{1/2}$. We further prove a matching minimax lower bound that holds under the same conditions. The reduction is computationally efficient whenever the finite-variance subroutine is. We also obtain a distribution-free prediction guarantee under a bounded raw $α$-moment assumption on the response, and give an analogous $α$-agnostic reduction for mean estimation.

papers.title: Quantum Many-Body Scars from Operator Size
papers.summary: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose terms have fixed size in an operator basis, we identify polynomially many Krylov basis states that it annihilates and that, in the thermodynamic limit, become concentrated on a single size sector. The size operator splits them into a tower of equally spaced levels that gives rise to coherent revivals characterized by collective oscillations of energy across the two copies. We provide a concrete realization of this construction in two copies of a general $q$-body nearest-neighbor spin chain, and the SYK model.

papers.title: Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
papers.summary: Electron transport is typically described in terms of relaxation times, which measure how quickly Fermi-surface deformations decay. We show here that the thermopower of a two-dimensional Fermi liquid instead probes the structure of these deformations in the form of their local temperature change, which we call the thermal dressing. This structure leads to an overshoot of the thermopower over its hydrodynamic value $- s/(ne)$ with increasing wave vector, before it falls to half that value in the ballistic limit. At low temperatures, the excess thermopower does not have the linear-in-temperature scaling expected of a Fermi liquid, but decreases only logarithmically as $1/\ln(T_F/T)$ at optimal wave vector. The overshoot is caused by collinear scattering, which redistributes energy over the Fermi surface and induces the thermal dressing, the strength of which grows with the angular harmonic index $m$ of the deformation. In contrast to tomographic effects in the charge conductivity, this overshoot does not rely on an odd-even effect in quasiparticle lifetimes and defines a distinct thermographic transport regime. The thermopower overshoot survives realistic disorder and should be detectable in a thermocouple with high-mobility samples.

papers.title: Structure and relaxation of long-lived odd-parity modes in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
papers.summary: In two-dimensional Fermi liquids, odd-parity deformations of the Fermi surface relax anomalously slowly at a rate $\sim T^4$, where $T$ is the temperature. However, the leading-logarithmic prediction for the magnitude of this rate $\sim m^4 \ln m$, where $m$ is an angular harmonic index, exceeds exact-diagonalization results and the $\ln m$ scaling is not observed. We resolve this discrepancy by evaluating the 2D Fermi-liquid collision integral for general regular isotropic potentials to leading order in $T/T_F$, including the nonlogarithmic term beyond the $\ln(T_F/T)$ term. We find that the local temperature modulation of the odd mode, which we call the thermal dressing, suppresses relaxation by collinear scattering, with residual relaxation set by large-angle scattering. Such large-angle processes give corrections of order $\ln m/\ln(T_F/T)$ that are not small and must be resummed. We benchmark our results against exact-diagonalization calculations for constant interactions and find agreement over a range $m^2 T/T_F \lesssim 0.4$, and we provide closed-form results for the slowest odd-mode relaxation rate of a spin-polarized dipolar gas.

papers.title: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
papers.summary: The first stars formed out of light elements (H, He, and Li leftover from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis) and began the chemical enrichment of the Universe. Identifying this first-generation population of stars, known as Population III, and understanding their properties is one of the most ambitious goals of modern extragalactic astrophysics. We report the detection of He and H emission lines and extremely low Oxygen abundance in AMORE6, a strongly magnified galaxy at redshift z = 5.725, i.e. approximately one billion years after the Big Bang, with deep James Webb Space Telescope spectroscopy. He II lambda1640 and lambda4686 emission lines are detected at 16.7 sigma and 4.0 sigma significance, respectively. The observed He II-to-Hbeta ratios are consistent with predictions for extreme ionizing radiation fields and the low chemical compositions typical of Population III stars. Oxygen abundance of the interstellar medium is estimated to be 8 x 10^-4 solar from weak [OIII]lambda4363 and lambda5008 lines, consistent with an almost pristine environment, perhaps enriched by the Pop III stars themselves. Although we cannot exclude alternative sources of hard ionizing radiation, such as accreting black holes, these observations offer the first view of the extremely low metallicity environment where the Universe's first stars are predicted to be born. The data show that such pockets of pristine gas still exist one billion years after the Big Bang and that they are dominated by very massive stars.

papers.title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning
papers.summary: This study examines one-day-ahead forecasting of the S&P 500 closing level using a 2006-2025 dataset that includes fundamental price data, macroeconomic indicators, and engineered technical features. We benchmark three model families, namely linear regression, vanilla recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), within a unified preprocessing and chronological evaluation pipeline. A central contribution of this work is a methodological audit of common practices in the deep-learning-for-stock-prediction literature. We identify three sources of result inflation that frequently appear in published methodologies: wavelet-denoised evaluation targets, the absence of a naive persistence baseline, and best-of-N replicate reporting. We then re-evaluate all model families under a corrected protocol that controls for each. Performance is reported using root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, and the Pearson correlation coefficient, averaged across N = 30 independent replicates per configuration. We compare models on accuracy, stability across replicates, and architectural depth sensitivity, using the naive persistence forecast (predicting today's close as tomorrow's close) as a primary baseline against which all candidate models must demonstrate improvement.

papers.title: Observation of rotonic density enhancement at the boundary of a uniform dipolar superfluid
papers.summary: The collective excitations of a quantum liquid lie at the heart of its emergent behaviour. In many systems, the variation of excitation energy ${\varepsilon}$ with wavevector $k$ exhibits a softening at a characteristic lengthscale, which plays a key role in thermodynamics and transport. These excitations, termed rotons, often reflect an underlying tendency of the liquid to crystallize into a competing symmetry-broken state, such as the solid state of helium or the Wigner crystal of electrons in a magnetic field. More than $50$ years ago, it was predicted that rotons should manifest as emergent density oscillations at the fluid's boundary, but this effect has not been observed. Here, we realize an ultracold dipolar superfluid confined in a homogeneous trapping potential and directly confirm the emergence of rotonic density enhancement at its edge. This is accompanied by rotonic density fluctuations across the bulk, which are linked to the static edge structure via the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. Increasing the dipolar character leads to an azimuthal density modulation of the fluid's boundary, which we show to be analogous to the behaviour of a quasi-one-dimensional fluid confined in an annular optical potential.

papers.title: Nonperturbative Bounds on the Ground-State Energy of Lattice QED
papers.summary: We establish nonperturbative bounds on the ground-state energy of lattice quantum electrodynamics with naive fermions in Coulomb gauge, within the Gaussian photon approximation. Our central result is a spectral comparison theorem showing that, in the thermodynamic limit, the minimum fermionic energy density over all link configurations coincides with that of the trivial gauge configuration. The proof exploits a logarithmic determinant representation and dimensional reduction, without relying on reflection positivity, and applies to lattices of either parity. Combining this result with the positivity of the electromagnetic and Coulomb Hamiltonians, we derive an explicit lower bound on the interacting ground-state energy. Finite-lattice counterexamples show that the thermodynamic limit is essential.

papers.title: Hölder continuity of meromorphic functions and equisingularity
papers.summary: For a complex analytic variety and an exponent between zero and one, we study the sheaf of meromorphic functions that are locally Hölder continuous with that exponent for the outer metric. It sits between the structure sheaves of the seminormalization and of the Lipschitz saturation of Pham and Teissier. We prove that these sheaves are coherent and that only finitely many of them are distinct, the exponents at which they change being rational numbers governed by the Rees valuations of the ideal of a certain diagonal. Each exponent defines a Hölder saturation of the variety. We show that a variety whose Hölder saturation is smooth for some exponent larger than one third is itself smooth and that one third is sharp. For reduced curve germs we compute the Hölder saturations from the characteristic exponents of the branches and give explicit thresholds, in terms of classical invariants, at which they become the seminormalization, the Lipschitz saturation, or a curve of the same multiplicity. We prove that homeomorphic curves are bi-Hölder homeomorphic for some positive exponent, whereas bi-Hölder homeomorphisms with exponent close enough to one preserve the multiplicity. We then introduce the relative Hölder saturation of a family and prove that it specializes to the saturations of the fibers over a dense Zariski-open subset of the base. This leads to two notions of equisingularity for families of complex analytic varieties, Hölder equisingularity, defined by a bi-Hölder trivialization, and the stronger Hölder equisaturation, defined by the triviality of the relative saturation. For families of reduced curve germs we show that they interpolate between topological, Whitney and Lipschitz equisingularity, with explicit exponents depending only on the invariants of the special fiber.

papers.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
papers.summary: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.

papers.title: Soft--hard Bayesian inference in heavy-ion collisions
papers.summary: Bayesian analyses of jet quenching commonly constrain jet--medium interaction parameters using a fixed quark-gluon plasma (QGP) background obtained from a soft-sector calibration. This approach neglects uncertainty in the medium and prevents hard observables from providing additional constraints on its properties. We investigate these effects in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV using sequential Bayesian inference in a reduced three-parameter space. We vary the initial normalization and nucleon width of the medium together with the jet--medium coupling, combining JETSCAPE medium evolution with MATTER+LBT calculations of high-$p_T$ hadron and inclusive-jet suppression. We first constrain all three parameters using the hard observables alone, then incorporate a projected soft-sector posterior through sequential inference. We find that the hard observables are sensitive to the medium properties and reveal substantial correlations with the jet--medium coupling, reflecting their compensating effects on jet quenching. Propagating the soft-sector information shifts the preferred coupling relative to a fixed-medium extraction, with the update driven primarily by hadron-suppression measurements. Despite substantial differences in the medium parameters and coupling favored by hard-observable-only and sequential inference, their suppression predictions remain similar over much of the measured range. These findings highlight the difficulty of distinguishing changes in the QGP medium from changes in microscopic jet--medium interaction strength using inclusive suppression measurements alone.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures. Contribution to the proceedings of Hard Probes 2026 (Nashville, Tennessee, 21-26 June 2026)

papers.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
papers.summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions. We curated 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions so that researchers can compare seven EEG feature families on the same time intervals for each participant and task. The dataset links continuous signals to precomputed measurements from 115 feature definitions or templates and records the quality decisions made for each recording. Analyses must still account for repeated measurements within participants, residual artefacts and differences between acquisition systems. Technical validation covered signal integrity, numerical checks on feature estimators and completeness of the released files. In every task, the median proportion of recording time retained after preprocessing was 100%. To illustrate reuse, we report saved participant-held-out evaluations comparing XGBoost using all seven families on eight-second windows with a predictor based only on recruitment-group prevalence in the training fold. Recruitment-group discrimination was stronger in Robots than in the three Slackline conditions. These descriptive results from overlapping cohorts do not establish diagnostic validity. The dataset, curation software and aggregate results for the predictive example are publicly available.
papers.comment: 28 pages, 7 figures. EEG dataset (v1.0.0): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21982978 EEG preprocessing and feature extraction software with XGBoost example (v1.1.0): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24399993

papers.title: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
papers.summary: We analyze a fully discrete finite element projection method for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and multiplicative noise. We show solvability and uniform moment estimates for the intermediate and the corrected velocity approximations under the assumption that the initial data is square-integrable and divergence free, and that the deterministic forcing term is bounded in $L^{q}(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ for a sufficiently large $q$. Under standard stability and approximation assumptions on the finite element spaces and a coupling condition on the spatial and temporal discretization parameters, we prove convergence of a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations. The analysis combines the complementary spatial and temporal estimates of the predicted and the corrected velocity approximations and uses the numerical dissipation to identify their common limit. We establish tightness of the piecewise constant temporal interpolations of the velocity field approximations using Aldous' criterion combined with the uniform discrete moment estimates. The convergence result holds in two and three space dimensions as it does not rely on any additional regularity of the limiting martingale solution beyond the one naturally available from the energy inequality. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the scheme in numerical experiments in two space dimensions for smooth and vortex sheet initial data.

papers.title: A proof of the polygonal Faber--Krahn inequality
papers.summary: We prove that, for every integer $n\ge3$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence, among simple polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides. We also obtain the optimal linear correction when fewer than $n$ sides are present. The proof combines a partition into convex cells with a mixed boundary comparison. Among convex polygons of fixed area and fixed sum of base angles less than $π$, the isosceles triangle minimizes the first eigenvalue with Dirichlet conditions on the base and Neumann conditions elsewhere. A comparison of Fourier transforms of conformal area densities proves this inequality and the corresponding upper bounds for inverse spectral moments of integer order at least two. We prove strict log-convexity of an interpolation of the eigenvalues of regular polygons of unit area for real parameters at least four. We then derive sharp hexagonal bounds for periodic convex polygonal tilings and asymptotic bounds for convex polygonal partitions of a fixed convex polygon, with an explicit correction for boundary junctions.

papers.title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design
papers.summary: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates. Each gate returns a status and an evidence record; on failure, the Skill records the earliest blocker, revises one bounded parameter group, and reruns the cheaper gates. The agent generates, validates, and trains autonomously within declared bounds, and escalates trade-offs, plateaus, and conflicting evidence to a human who sets the next design direction. An evidence-driven design trajectory for bidirectional in-hand manipulation yielded SAGE Hand (Skill-Aware Generative Embodiment): four fingers, 16 actuated DoF, an integrated guiding palm, compact roots, cylindrical tips, and a collision-cleared opposable thumb. Under a matched training protocol, SAGE Hand reaches 45.6% task success on a hexagonal prism against 37.3% for the LEAP hand, and 70.8% on a bicolor cylinder against 51.6%. Dense simulated tactile input more than halves the cylinder drop rate. In a controlled iteration study, the Skill path preserves capture at 164/165 trials while the path without the Skill degrades to 14/165, confirming that the gates act as a regression guard during refinement. Accepted candidates pack with URDF/MJCF, metrics, checkpoints, and a provenance manifest.

papers.title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
papers.summary: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.

papers.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
papers.summary: To prevent motion sensors from acting as covert microphones, Android 12+ caps SensorManager gyroscope and accelerometer rates at 200 Hz by default, requires HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS for higher rates, and throttles sensors back to 200 Hz when the microphone toggle is off. We show that Android's Camera2 subsystem bypasses these defenses. During an active Camera2 session, Camera HAL stabilization pipelines record high-rate gyroscope measurements and export them via vendor CaptureResult metadata. Loudspeaker speech excites chassis vibrations that couple into this path. Across 50 smartphones (2020-2026) from 10 vendors, 37 expose gyroscope metadata via Camera2, and 26 exceed 200 Hz--including six flagship models at 800-1000 Hz, double SensorManager's 400-500 Hz ceiling. This channel requires neither RECORD_AUDIO nor HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS and defeats privacy switches: turning off the microphone toggle does not throttle metadata, and turning off the camera toggle blanks only video frames while 800-1000 Hz metadata keeps streaming. To build a zero-profiling attack that generalizes to unseen phones, we introduce Source-to-Leakage Learning (S2L). Prior attacks train on real sensor traces, entangling speech with a specific phone's mechanical resonances and sampling rate. S2L decouples speech content from hardware acoustics using a physics-constrained forward simulator. Trained exclusively on simulated leakage without target-phone traces, our universal recognizer CamEar achieves 52.1% mean word accuracy (up to 61.8%) and 74.3% character accuracy (up to 80.7%) across the six 800-1000 Hz phones. In contrast, ISpyU models fine-tuned on real target-phone data drop to 25.9% word accuracy on unseen phones; CamEar improves cross-device accuracy by 101.4% and outperforms ISpyU's same-device models on every tested phone.

papers.title: Non-penetrating World Models
papers.summary: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent. Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%. Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles. We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights. Project Page: https://nopeworld.github.io .

papers.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
papers.summary: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside. We evaluate Model Carving by pre-training standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers from 140M to 1.3B. At equal training compute, carved models reach a lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Furthermore, carved models also outperform size-matched models produced by pruning or distillation, suggesting that the best way to obtain small models for edge devices is to carve them during training, not to compress a large one afterwards. This advantage both grows with scale and carries over to downstream tasks such as few-shot evaluation and generation. Because the removed sublayers no longer run, carved models also cost up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and decode up to 1.6 times faster without cost in quality. Our results show that architecture, like weights, should be learned and not fixed in advance, and that inside every large transformer is a smaller, faster, stronger one waiting to be carved out.
papers.comment: 38 pages, 15 figures, 19 tables. Under review at ICLR 2027. Project page: https://kadenzheng.com/model-carving/

papers.title: Explicational statistics: research for an AI age
papers.summary: AI is dramatically changing the statistical research landscape. I argue that production of a distinct category of statistical knowledge, which I refer to as explicational statistics, is actually becoming more valuable as AI increasingly automates other parts of the research process. I define explicational statistics, contextualize it in terms of other forms of statistical knowledge, and explain why I think the rise of AI makes it more valuable. I demonstrate my framework by first developing a new dimension reduction method, Ambient Embedding Projection, that can simultaneously visualize the intrinsic geometry of a data manifold along with how that manifold is embedded into ambient space. I then use my new method to conceive of a new statistical property of a collection of manifolds, related to metric distortion, that in single-cell biology can capture the ensemble behavior of cell populations. I apply these ideas to single-nuclei RNA-seq data from the brains of mice from different behavioral conditions to reveal potential cellular mechanisms of chronic social defeat stress.

papers.title: Receptor Abundance Alone Underpredicts Red Blood Cell Adhesion in Gaucher Disease
papers.summary: Red blood cells (RBCs) in Gaucher disease (GD) adhere abnormally to vessel walls and carry more Lutheran/basal cell adhesion molecule (Lu/BCAM), a laminin receptor. Whether receptor abundance sets this adhesion is untested. We simulated RBCs carrying stochastic Lu/BCAM-laminin bonds, calibrated a population on control donors, and predicted GD adhesion from the 1.3-fold receptor rise. On laminin and endothelium the data exceed the prediction 1.6- to 1.7-fold. Matching them requires 2.4- and 4.6-fold more binding-competent receptors, compatible with the estimated 5.7-fold rise in phosphorylated receptors. Neither a stiffer membrane nor higher bond affinity removes the shortfall at high shear stress. In sickle cell disease, given active-receptor counts, the model predicts the fall in adhesion under hydroxyurea within 1.4-fold, while total receptors rise. Adhesion likely follows receptor state more than abundance. Stiffening instead retains cells at a splenic slit.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures. Supplementary Materials (32 pages) and Movies S1 and S2 are ancillary files

papers.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
papers.summary: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is essential for high predictive performance, but its computational cost becomes prohibitive when candidate configurations require repeated training on large datasets. This paper proposes a ranking-preserving coreset (RPC) selection framework for accelerating evolutionary HPO. The method constructs a compact coreset that preserves the relative ranking of hyperparameter configurations observed on the full training data. Coreset selection is formulated as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes Spearman rank correlation between full-data and subset-based configuration rankings while penalizing subset size. The selected coreset is then used for HPO with three evolutionary algorithms: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Cross-generational elitist Selection, Heterogeneous Recombination and Cataclysmic Mutation (CHC), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Experiments on seven tabular, two text, and two image benchmark datasets show that RPC substantially reduces HPO time while maintaining test accuracy comparable to full-dataset HPO across decision tree, text classification, and image classification tasks. Across datasets and optimizers, HPO-stage speedups range from approximately 1.14x to 8.80x, while the one-time coreset construction cost is accounted for separately through end-to-end runtime and break-even analysis. On 20 held-out configurations excluded from coreset construction, RPC achieves higher ranking correlation than same-size random sampling on 8 of 11 datasets (dataset-level Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p = 0.014). These results show that ranking preservation extends beyond the configurations used during selection. The one-time construction cost can be amortized when the coreset is reused across HPO runs.

papers.title: Differential Transmutations and First-Passage Expansions for Monomial Brownian Boundaries
papers.summary: Let $P_t=\exp(t\partial_x^2/2)$ be the heat semigroup and let $F(t)=ρt^p$, where $p\ge2$ is an integer. Previous transported-zero theory associates with this boundary a constant-flux solution annihilated by a polynomial-coefficient differential operator of order $2p-1$. We show that the same differential structure contains the complete formal perturbation expansion of the Brownian first-passage density to $F$. For $N=2p-1$ we construct graded spatial operators \[ \mathcal A_r^{(p)}x^n= \frac{(-1)^r}{r!} \frac{\prod_{j=0}^{pr-1}(n+2j+1)} {\prod_{j=1}^{Nr}(n+j)}x^{n+Nr} \] and prove the Laplace conjugacy \[ \mathscr L\mathcal A_r^{(p)}\mathscr L^{-1} =\frac{(-1)^r}{r!}k^r \left(-\frac1k\frac{d}{dk}\right)^{pr}. \] Consequently, the inverse spatial transmutation applied to a reflected Dirac mass generates, coefficient by coefficient, the unique formal solution of the exponential-martingale transform equation for first passage. The cubic case is developed explicitly and checked algebraically through fifth order. We also explain how this differential construction and the independently developed Wright--Volterra generalized-image construction represent the same first-passage law in different coordinates. The present result is formal at all orders; convergence of the resulting perturbation series is left as a separate analytic problem.

papers.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
papers.summary: Small modular reactors (SMRs) are being considered as compact, high-energy-density power sources for future all-electric ships. In such systems, propulsion-load variations can propagate through the electrical network, turbine-generator set, steam generator, and reactor, producing coupled nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical transients. This paper presents an integrated dynamic load-following analysis of an SMR-powered all-electric ship with and without battery energy storage system (BESS) support. The model couples an integral pressurized water reactor, a once-through moving-boundary steam generator, a simplified turbine model, a synchronous generator, an AC shipboard electrical network, an asynchronous propulsion motor, and a grid-connected BESS. A propulsion-load reduction is applied through the motor torque command, and the responses of the SMR-alone and SMR+BESS configurations are compared. The results show that, without BESS support, the sudden decrease in propulsion motor power creates a temporary surplus between turbine mechanical power and electrical demand, causing a large over-frequency transient and rapid steam-cycle adjustment. With BESS support, the battery absorbs excess electrical power during the transient, reducing the frequency peak from approximately 61.1 Hz to about 60.06 Hz. The BESS also indirectly smooths the upstream steam-cycle and reactor responses, including steam flow, steam-generator pressure, feedwater flow, coolant temperature, reactivity, reactor thermal power, and steam-generator region lengths. These results demonstrate the importance of modeling nuclear-powered electric ships as coupled multi-domain systems and show that BESS integration can improve short-term load-following performance.
papers.journal: International Congress on Advances in Nuclear Power Plants (ICAPP 2026), Phoenix, AZ, November 15-18, 2026

papers.title: Molecular structure breaks universality in screening behavior of electrolyte solutions
papers.summary: Electrostatic screening is one of the most fundamental phenomena in electrolyte solutions. While dilute electrolytes are described by the universal Debye--Hückel theory, recent experiments have reported an apparently universal scaling law for screening lengths in concentrated electrolytes, fueling ongoing debate over anomalous underscreening. Yet, liquid state theory has been unable to determine whether molecular details of the solvent, the ions, or both should preserve or break such universality. Using machine-learned classical density functional theory, we compute numerically exact decay lengths across a hierarchy of electrolyte models of increasing molecular complexity. We find that molecular details qualitatively reshape screening: solvent attraction generates a new monotonic decay mode, solvent polarity produces re-entrant behavior, and ionic structure alone can drastically alter screening-length exponents. Consequently, no single scaling law describes screening universally across these molecularly distinct electrolytes. Our results challenge equilibrium interpretations of experimentally observed universality in concentrated electrolytes.
papers.comment: Main: 11 pages, 4 figures. SI: 12 pages, 1 figure

papers.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
papers.summary: Buoyancy glitches in red giants provide localized information on the interior structure near the base of the convective envelope, but their properties are typically inferred from dedicated seismic modelling rather than global properties, limiting large-sample applications. We investigate whether the buoyancy-glitch amplitude ($A_g$), location ($W_{\rm g}^{\star}$), and width ($D_g$) can be recovered from global stellar properties using gradient-boosted tree regressors (XGBoost and LightGBM). The models were trained on a grid of 12580 synthetic stellar models of low-luminosity red giants, with target parameters derived from fits to the local buoyancy frequency profile. We find that $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ exhibit excellent recoverability, achieving test-set $\mathcal{R}^2$ values of 0.98 and 0.97, respectively. In contrast, $A_g$ shows moderate recoverability overall ($\mathcal{R}^2=0.68$). This reduced recoverability of $A_g$ is concentrated in the large frequency separation range $Δν= 4.6$--$18.9\,μ$Hz, where the glitch resides in the evanescent-zone transition between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity, increasing intrinsic scatter. SHAP analysis shows that $ν_{\rm max}$ and $T_{\rm eff}$ dominate the predictions across all targets, indicating that the regressors rely primarily on evolutionary state. While $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ are tightly constrained by global evolutionary trends, the lower recoverability of $A_g$ reflects localized structural complexity associated with red-giant evolution. Overall, for the synthetic grid adopted here, these results indicate that global properties provide a direct estimate of the buoyancy-glitch parameters and a way to prioritise dedicated mixed-mode inversions for large asteroseismic samples such as Kepler and PLATO.

papers.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
papers.summary: Neuromorphic sensing and computing offer a promising alternative to conventional deep learning pipelines for mobile robots, where perception must run continuously under tight latency and energy constraints. However, most neuromorphic solutions are still evaluated offline or on isolated benchmarks, and their integration into complete robotic systems remains largely unexplored. In this technical report, a four-wheel rover platform is presented that combines three real-time perception pipelines: a classical audio tagging pipeline based on Pretrained Audio Neural Networks (PANNs) running on an NVIDIA Jetson GPU, a neuromorphic audio pipeline in which a spiking neural network (SNN) is deployed on the SynSense Xylo Audio~2 chip, and a neuromorphic vision pipeline in which events from an event-based camera are processed by the SpikeYOLO spiking detector for traffic cone detection. On the Xylo chip, the whole processing chain---from the microphone signal to the classification of low- and high-pitched sounds---is performed on-chip, while the host only configures the device and reads the output neurons. All models are deployed as containerised services and integrated through ROS~2, and a configurable action dispatcher maps the detected classes to robot behaviours, closing the loop between perception and actuation. The platform is demonstrated in a proof-of-concept scenario in which the robot reacts to sound classes detected by both audio pipelines and detects traffic cones with the event camera, showing the feasibility of integrating neuromorphic hardware into a multimodal robotic platform operating in real time.

papers.title: Atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances of young stars with APOGEE -- II. Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, and Sulphur abundances in Orion
papers.summary: We derived the abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, and iron in young G-, K-, and M-type stars (effective temperatures of 3500--5900 K) using APOGEE-2 infrared spectra. Our final sample comprises 195 slow rotators ($v\sin i$ $\leq$ 30 km~s$^{-1}$) in the Orion complex (Orion A, B, OB1, and $λ$~Ori). The abundances were determined using MARCS model atmospheres, atmospheric parameters derived with \tona, and the \bacc\ code. We obtained median abundances of $ε$(C) = 8.37$\pm$0.10, $ε$(N) = 7.35$\pm$0.16, $ε$(O) = 8.63$\pm$0.08, $ε$(S) = 7.19$\pm$0.18, and $ε$(Fe) = 7.45$\pm$0.05. Nitrogen is subsolar ([N/H] $=-0.48$), whereas carbon, oxygen, sulphur, and iron are within 0.1 dex of the solar values. We find no spatial structure within the Orion subgroups, and the only significant difference is a 0.29 dex lower nitrogen abundance in Orion A than in Orion OB1, which does not extend to the other elements. Compared with 430 nearby main-sequence stars analysed in the same way, Orion shows carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen abundances lower by 0.1--0.2 dex, although consistent within the errors, whereas sulphur and iron differ by less than 0.07 dex. We also compare our abundances with nebular abundances of HII regions and star-forming galaxies: the stellar abundances of oxygen, sulphur, and iron are higher, with the largest offset in iron, although the agreement in abundance ratios improves when temperature inhomogeneities and dust depletion are taken into account.
papers.comment: 22 pages, 6 Figures, 6 Tables. Accepted in MNRAS

papers.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
papers.summary: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage. On NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches 97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$ under pure task loss ($α=0$) and 98.83% at $α=0.05$ (matched by $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU at $α=0.05$, vs. 80.60% at $α=0$), while softmax-gated hub OT drops to 3.52%. In bidirectional operator microbenchmarks, our kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262\mathrm{K}$ (2.2x faster with 4.0x smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax) and 1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention at $L=4{,}096$; multi-layer LM runs use the unfused path. Zero-shot WikiText-103 multi-needle retrieval hits 100.00% (128/128 queries at $L=65\mathrm{K}$) vs. 0.78% for short-trained RoPE FlashAttention, and compact 4-layer WikiText-4K runs show modest causal and masked LM gains.

papers.title: Minkowski Correlation Functions (MCF): Long-range, robust shape descriptors for point patterns
papers.summary: A morphometric analysis of point patterns using Minkowski functionals is short-sighted, whereas correlation functions do not provide robust, i.e., additive shape descriptors. To combine the advantages of both standard techniques and to overcome their weaknesses, we introduce ring-based Minkowski correlation functions (MCFs) as robust and sensitive descriptors of disordered point patterns. By assigning to each point a spherical shell and quantifying the resulting two-phase morphology via Minkowski functionals, MCFs capture structural information across multiple length scales, remain sensitive at radii where conventional disk-based Minkowski functionals have saturated, and implicitly encode higher-order correlations beyond the pair correlation and structure factor. We present an exact and efficient algorithm for planar patterns extending the established disk-based morphological approach to long ranges. Applications across scales -- active colloids (Quincke rollers), longleaf pine trees, and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field -- demonstrate clear and systematic deviations from homogeneous Poisson references, with distinct responses of covered area, boundary length, and Euler characteristic. The approach combines short computation times, robustness to noise, and straightforward edge handling with clear interpretability as low-dimensional functions of the outer ring radius.

papers.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes
papers.summary: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{-1,+1,\star\}^{\mathcal X}$ be a partial concept class of finite VC dimension $d$. We construct a deterministic agnostic PAC learner that, for every $\varepsilon,δ\in(0,1)$, uses $O((d+\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon^2)$ i.i.d. examples from an arbitrary distribution $\mathcal D$ over $\mathcal X\times\{-1,+1\}$ and returns a total concept $\hat h:\mathcal X\to\{-1,+1\}$ satisfying $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(\hat h)\leq \min_{h\in\mathcal H}\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)+\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-δ$, where $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)=\mathbb P_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal D}[h(x)\neq y]$. This establishes the optimal sample complexity, matching the lower bound of Alon et al. (FOCS 2021).

papers.title: Probing CP violation in weak radiative and dielectron decays of $Λ$ and $Ξ^-$ hyperons
papers.summary: The rare decays $Λ\to ne^+e^-$ and $Ξ^-\toΣ^-e^+e^-$ can serve as sensitive probes of $CP$ violation, especially that induced by interactions from beyond the standard model. We demonstrate that this is so because the dominant long-distance components of these processes provide sizable absorptive phases that can give rise to significant $CP$ violation via interference with potential new-physics effects. Treating the new contributions model-independently, we find that this leads to $CP$-odd rate asymmetries that are currently allowed by kaon and hyperon data to reach the 10% and 20% levels in the $Λ$ and $Ξ^-$ cases, respectively. Interestingly, we obtain comparable outcomes for the related weak radiative modes $Λ\to nγ$ and $Ξ^-\toΣ^-γ$. These results are testable at future high-statistics hyperon facilities.

papers.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
papers.summary: The performance of Rydberg-atom receivers is seldom stated as a radio-frequency (RF) link budget. The receiver is shown to be an intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical link whose modulator is the laser-driven vapor. The transmission of a warm vapor is derived in closed form by averaging the four-level response over atomic velocities. The conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, intercept points, and spurious-free dynamic range follow from this one function. For a weak probe the instantaneous bandwidth is half the width of the transparency window in two-photon detuning. The local-oscillator beat places the second-order intercept near twice the local-oscillator field, so the local oscillator sets the even-order linearity. For a rubidium transition at 17.04 GHz the closed forms agree with a velocity-resolved density-matrix model to 1% for the slope and the intercepts and to 10% for the bandwidth. They underestimate the group delay by a third. The response is tied to atomic constants, and the sensing volume escapes the Chu limit. However, the noise figure of a warm vapor rules it out as a general replacement for an antenna and low-noise amplifier.

papers.title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
papers.summary: Sinusoidal blade pitching can improve vertical-axis turbine performance, but whether a blade could follow the same motion passively depends on the energy exchanged through pitching. This study experimentally examines 480 prescribed-pitch conditions using a single-blade model following a circular trajectory in a water channel at four tip-speed ratios (TSRs) from 1.25 to 3.14. The amplitude associated with the highest measured power decreases from 16° to 12° and then 8° as TSR increases, with the corresponding phase shifting from 0 to pi/4. At TSRs of 1.25 and 3.14, the cycle-averaged power coefficient increases from 0.0047 to 0.1037 and from 0.4698 to 0.5948, respectively. Pitching-energy maps show nearly neutral net hydrodynamic pitching work for the highest-performing motions at the two lower TSRs and net energy transfer from the flow to pitching at the two higher TSRs. Virtual damping narrows the positive-energy region, although the higher-TSR best-tested motions retain an energy surplus at nonzero damping. However, net energy transfer from the flow to pitching also occurs for motions with substantial power losses. At the lowest TSR, phase-resolved force measurements and particle image velocimetry link the gain to delayed dynamic-stall-vortex formation and shedding, prolonged favorable loading, and reduced subsequent negative power. At the highest TSR, the flow and loading change locally, with little alteration of the main power-producing event. The joint maps identify performance-enhancing motions with an energetic margin against assumed dissipation, providing candidates for further passive or assisted pitching studies.

papers.title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
papers.summary: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.

papers.title: What Must a Model Tell a Planner? Outcome Interfaces for Risk-Aware Planning After Robot Damage
papers.summary: When a robot is damaged, it must decide which routes it can still afford, and the amount of risk it may accept can change from one mission to the next. We argue that whether a learned model helps such a robot depends on its decision interface, that is, on what the model hands to the planner. A decision policy tells the planner what to do, whereas an outcome model, a kind of world model, predicts the consequences of each route. We study simulated Unitree Go2 quadrupeds and H1 humanoids with weakened motors, added payloads, or reduced foot friction. We compare four interfaces. The first is a decision policy, and the second is the same policy trained with fixed penalties for infeasible routes. The third is an outcome model that predicts the feasibility and travel time of each route. The fourth, which we call a capability contract, is an outcome model that predicts the chance of success and the travel time of the robot on each terrain and composes them along a route. All share the same collected experience, matched tuning and risk calibration, and an uncertainty guard. Two comparatively low-risk probes let the capability contract rank hazardous terrains about as well as four new trials on every hazard. At a calibrated 5% limit on selecting empirically infeasible routes, outcome models cut declined missions from about 32% to 7-8% on Go2 and from 57% to 35-36% on H1 compared with the plain policy. Fixed penalties narrow this gap, but the best penalty changes with the risk target. Predicting outcomes lets the planner preserve missions by changing routes as risk requirements tighten.

papers.title: Intervals of limit points for $B_α$-spectral radii
papers.summary: For a finite simple graph $G$, let \[ B_α(G)=αA(G)+(1-α)L(G)=(1-α)D(G)+(2α-1)A(G),\qquad 0\leq α\leq 1. \] We study the limit points of the spectral radii of these matrices. Put $a_α=1-α$, $b_α=|2α-1|$, and $w_α=a_α+b_α$. We prove that, for every $α\neq 1/2$ and every integer $d\geq 3$, the interval \[ \left[a_αd+2b_α\sqrt{d-1},\,w_αd\right] \] consists entirely of $B_α$-limit points. All these points are realized by connected bipartite graphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We extend the induced-subgraph interpolation of Alon and Wei from $A$ to $aD+bA$, and obtain a unified proof using bipartite Ramanujan graphs. Consecutive intervals overlap for large $d$; hence the set of $B_α$-limit points contains a half-line for every $α\neq 1/2$. At $α=1/2$, one has $B_{1/2}=D/2$, and the set of spectral radii is discrete. Combining uniform edge subdivisions with generalized Bethe decorations, we improve the Laplacian and signless Laplacian half-line to $[29/5,\infty)$, verified by an exact rational certificate. We also treat two complementary tree constructions. For the starlike trees $T_{1,m,m}$, the limiting $B_α$-spectral radius is the unique solution above the path threshold of an explicit unsquared equation. More generally, letting selected arms of a starlike tree tend to infinity produces ordered limit points with tree realizations. Finally, we give the exact affine relations among $B_α$, the $A_β$-matrix, and the deformed Laplacian. These identify which tree and caterpillar results are reparametrizations of earlier work. The interval theorem also yields half-lines of $A_β$-limit points for every $0\leβ<1$, and of deformed-Laplacian limit points for every nonzero deformation parameter.

papers.title: Star Triangulations
papers.summary: We study full triangulations of planar point configurations consisting of $n$ points in convex position and one point in the interior, assuming that no three points are collinear (star configurations). Our main contribution is a classification of the star configurations up to combinatorial equivalence. We show that there are $2^{n-1}-n$ equivalence classes, by establishing a bijection between a star configuration and a particular Young diagram. By transforming each such Young diagram to a binary sequence, we manage to also give a combinatorial description of the orbits of these star configurations under the dihedral group action, encoding each such orbit through a black-and-white bracelet. For each star configuration, we derive an explicit formula for the number of its full triangulations, expressed in terms of Catalan numbers and the parts of the associated Young diagram. Additionally we derive a formula of these full triangulations expressed only in terms of Catalan numbers and the bead structure of the associated bracelet. Finally, we let the points move freely under the restriction that they stay in a star configuration and show that there exist $\binom{2n-3}{n-3}$ topologically distinct full triangulations.

papers.title: Ehrhard-Type inequalities for radial measures
papers.summary: We study Ehrhard-type inequalities for convex sets under rotationally invariant probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge2$, described by a radial density profile $\varphi$. We give sufficient conditions on the profile that apply to Gaussian and multivariate Student measures, including the Cauchy measure, and to a family of mixtures of two Student measures. We also prove necessary conditions on the profile and its tails. Together, these conditions determine the exact parameter range for this mixture family and characterize the rotationally invariant stable measures satisfying the inequality.

papers.title: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
papers.summary: We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter. We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k\geq 3$ no polynomial-time approximation or hardness is known, even for diverse spanning trees. We show that sampling $k\geq 3$ bases provides a tight $Θ(\log k)$ approximation. We then combine structural insights about the local density of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ with classical LP-rounding techniques to obtain a polynomial-time $1/6$-approximation algorithm for the $k$-diversity problem in arbitrary matroids, the first constant-factor polynomial-time approximation for max--min diversity on any matroid. A key ingredient for our result is the \emph{Farthest Matroid Basis} problem: given a collection of bases, find a new basis as far as possible from all of them. We give a polynomial-time $1/3$-approximation algorithm for this, which is our main algorithmic primitive for $k$ max--min diversity. We also show it is $W[1]$-hard when parameterized by the optimal distance. We also improve the $1/6$-approximation for $k$-diversity, for partition matroids and graphic matroids of constant arboricity.

papers.title: Mammalian gonadal development: origins, specification and differentiation of ovary and testis cell lineages
papers.summary: Testicular and ovarian development requires the coordinated formation and assembly of multiple cell types that enable these organs to fulfill their roles in sexual differentiation, reproduction, and endocrine function. A defining feature of gonadal development is that both testes and ovaries arise from a common bipotential primordium, the genital ridge, composed of multipotent progenitors. In this Review, we synthesize current knowledge on the origin, specification, differentiation, and function of the major fetal gonadal somatic lineages, drawing primarily on mouse and human studies. We describe how the adrenogonadal primordium (AGP) gives rise to the gonadal primordium (GP), how coelomic epithelium-derived progenitors generate the supporting, steroidogenic/stromal, and supporting-like cell lineages, and how these progenitors become progressively fate-restricted. We highlight recent evidence for early lineage priming within spatially organized domains of the coelomic epithelium. We further examine the molecular pathways and cellular processes governing sex-specific differentiation of these lineages and discuss remaining gaps in our understanding of how bipotential gonads differentiate into testes or ovaries, and their implication for human health.

papers.title: Interactive Semi-Parametric On-Track Learning for Vehicle Dynamics in Autonomous Racing
papers.summary: Autonomous racing requires an accurate vehicle dynamics model near the limits of handling, yet a mismatch between the nominal and actual dynamics inevitably remains. To reduce this mismatch, existing methods learn from on-track data, i.e., data collected while the vehicle drives on the track under racing conditions, by adapting the physical parameters of the nominal model or by learning a residual that captures the remaining mismatch. However, these on-track learning methods typically handle either the physical parameters or the residual separately, which restricts their ability to resolve the mismatch. To address this limitation, we propose an interactive semi-parametric learning framework that learns both the physical parameters and the residual under a single shared prediction-error objective. Since updating one changes the learning target of the other, they are recursively updated in turn, each guided by the other's latest update. Each update is then accepted only if it does not increase the shared objective, so that the objective is guaranteed to be non-increasing and convergent over the recursion. Numerical simulations and hardware experiments show that the proposed framework outperforms the baselines. Compared with the nominal model, it reduces the one-step prediction errors of lateral velocity and yaw rate by 90.0% and 81.6% in simulation and by 54.0% and 59.4% on hardware.

papers.title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
papers.summary: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them. We present DiTraR, which addresses video selection from two complementary directions. A witness-interval scorer decomposes the query into probes and scores every candidate interval of every corpus video exactly; a multi-scorer energy ensemble averages the energies of independently trained scorers before one exhaustive search; and a transcript verifier, a frozen language model that reads the time-stamped dialogue of the highest-ranked videos, re-orders the moments without changing their boundaries. With all settings frozen on development data and a single evaluation, DiTraR reaches 24.36 and 13.55 R@1 at IoU 0.5 and 0.7 on the TVR validation split. The ensemble improves queries about visual content, the verifier improves queries about dialogue, and their gains largely add up.

papers.title: A Coats-Based Formulation for Multiphase Reactive Transport Accounting for Aqueous Phase Disappearance
papers.summary: As part of the energy transition, underground hydrogen (H2) storage in porous media has emerged as an alternative solution for large-scale energy storage to salt caverns. Assessing the feasibility of such systems and ensuring their operation requires accurate modeling of the geochemical processes that may alter the composition of the stored gas. This results in a highly nonlinear coupled system of partial differential equations, ordinary differential equations, and algebraic constraints, calling for robust and specialized numerical strategies. In this work, we adopt a Globally Implicit Approach (GIA), as sequential solution algorithms are known to introduce splitting errors due to the decoupling of flow and geochemical processes. In addition, most splitting-based methods implicitly assume the persistent presence of the liquid phase, an assumption that may be violated during gas injection or withdrawal owing to aqueous phase vaporization and mineral precipitation in the vicinity of wells. We extend Coats' formulation to multiphase reactive transport with a rigorous and fully implicit management of aqueous phase disappearance and reappearance. The proposed approach introduces new molar concentration unknowns for basis species that track the re-appearance of the aqueous phase and guarantee the nonsingularity of the Jacobian matrix. Additionally, the appearance of the liquid phase is managed using a multiphase flash calculation algorithm. The proposed algorithm is validated against the CO2 storage benchmark problems. Finally, the approach is applied to an underground H2 storage in an aquifer under cyclic injection and withdrawal conditions.

papers.title: Optimal High-Dimensional Martingale CLTs over Rectangles
papers.summary: We prove Gaussian approximation bounds over rectangles for high-dimensional martingale sums, with lower bounds showing optimality up to powers of $\log n$. The results cover bounded increments, conditional and marginal sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential tails, and uniform $q$th-moment bounds on the largest absolute coordinate for $2<q\le3$. The predictable quadratic variation $Q$ may be random; the comparison Gaussian has deterministic covariance $Σ=\mathbb{E}Q$. We assume $Σ_{jj}=1$ and $\max_j\sum_k|Σ_{jk}|^s\le M$ for fixed $s>0$ and $M\ge1$, allowing $Σ$ to be singular, and quantify the error due to $Q-Σ$. Conditional tail bounds yield the same dimension threshold as boundedness, whereas marginal tail bounds give smaller thresholds. We also establish necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform convergence in all these classes; under the uniform moment assumption, the criterion holds for every fixed $q>2$. When $Q=I_d$, the bounded and marginal light-tail rates have no additional factors in $\log n$ if $\log(ed)\ge\{\log(en)\}^2$; the same holds for the finite-moment rates with $2<q\le3$ in every dimension, for all sufficiently large $n$.

papers.title: Transpilation-Aware Multi-Vendor QPU Scheduling with Predicted Post-Transpilation Fidelity
papers.summary: Cluster schedulers already choose nodes, GPUs and accelerators for submitted workloads, enforce quotas and spread load. QPUs from several vendors are now schedulable resources in the same clusters, yet the user still names the device, usually the one with the best average fidelity. For a given circuit that choice is often wrong: compiling onto each device's qubit connectivity adds gates, so a job can meet its required success probability on one device and miss it on another with similar error rates, and checking this exactly by compiling for every candidate is too slow for a scheduling decision. We let the scheduler choose the QPU in two stages. A training-free estimate predicts, in milliseconds and without compiling, the success probability on every candidate and filters out those that would miss the requirement; only the chosen device then compiles the circuit, re-checks it, and binds the job or rolls back. The estimate matches compiling every candidate at about 25x lower latency in simulation, ranks measured success on IBM hardware as well as the post-compilation estimate (Spearman rho = 0.95), reduces requirement violations from tens of jobs to a few, and avoids them under contention without piling jobs onto one device. Across vendors it works when error rates are comparable (IBM and IQM) and fails when published figures overstate a device.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 11 figures, 10 tables. Code, data and scripts to reproduce all experiments: https://github.com/anapaulaappel/QPUScheduler

papers.title: A quasi-tree expansion of the Homfly polynomial
papers.summary: The Homfly polynomial is one of the best-studied invariants of oriented links. Here, building on work of Jaeger and others, we present a new method of computing it. Terms in the expansion are algebraically simple and they are indexed by certain quasi-trees of the Seifert graph of an (almost) arbitrary link diagram. The quasi-trees, in turn, depend on a single basepoint along the link but no more auxiliary data. This allows us to streamline the proofs of some old results and to find new ones as well, such as an upper bound on the total degree in terms of directed joins of the Seifert graph.

papers.title: The Thurston algorithm for general entire maps on the complex plane: Existence and uniqueness
papers.summary: We prove that a marked topological entire Thurston map $(f,A)$ of stable parabolic type is Thurston equivalent relative to $A$ to a postsingularly finite entire function if and only if it has no Levy cycle relative to $A\cup\{\infty\}$. Here $A$ is a finite forward-invariant set containing the postsingular set. In the realizable case, the entire function is unique up to complex affine conjugacy, and every orbit of the Thurston pullback converges to its fixed point. We establish a Wolff--Denjoy type estimate for nonexpanding self-maps $T$ of the Teichmüller space of any connected orientable surface of finite type without boundary. If $T$ has an unbounded orbit, there are a nonzero measured foliation $G$ and a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}_{T^k x}(G)\le C\operatorname{Ext}_x(G)$ for every $x$ and $k\ge0$. For a fixed-point-free transcendental Thurston pullback, this supplies the foliation used in the existence proof. A central tool is a fixed finite measure obtained as the total-variation limit of renormalized pushforward measures transported back along a Teichmüller ray. It allows us to select a cylinder at a late time and compare the mass of the same marked region at different times. If $G$ has a cylinder, a four-point extremal-length estimate and the Thurston matrix force a Levy cycle. Otherwise, in the absence of a Levy cycle, cluster rescaling shows that cylinders of large modulus carry almost all the fixed measure at all late times. Following a cylinder of definite mass until its modulus decreases gives a contradiction. We compare this geometric argument with the proofs for real entire maps and exponential maps.

papers.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
papers.summary: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD). Trained on experimental and synthetic structures and extensive MD data, it supports multi-component systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions. Structure-prediction accuracy is comparable to top open-weight biomolecular folding models, and a context parallel mode enables prediction of megadalton complexes. Equilibrium distributions approximate MD references with free-energy errors near 1 kcal/mol across tested proteins and complexes. Time propagation predicts long-timescale dynamical trajectories and kinetics of binding and conformational changes. Generated structures can be controlled by conditioning on residue contacts or steering with user-defined bias potentials. Enhanced sampling enables free energy calculation involving rare states. BioEmu2 makes the study of biomolecular ensembles and dynamics scalable.

papers.title: The Fiscal and Economic Implications of Green Mandates: a Boltzmann Approach to Public Governance
papers.summary: Public authorities increasingly need to translate multifaceted policy objectives into concrete fiscal and investment choices while accounting for their socioeconomic consequences. A credible ex-ante impact assessment should report downstream implications attributable to the historical baseline and specified policy targets, without introducing discretionary assumptions about unknown administrative, socioeconomic or other physical processes. Bringing the large-scale perspective of statistical physics to public governance, we construct such an ex-ante impact assessment. Its scope encompasses policy objectives that condition a finite number of generalized moments of observables in the historical baseline, which comprises a sufficiently large collection of projects or public programmes. As a proof-of-principle application, we consider the green transition in the energy-generation sector using the historical baseline of many infrastructure projects from the World Bank. Our earlier results deriving closed-form expressions for coarse-grained combinatorial probabilities enable a tractable statistical and downstream assessment. We assess the statistical compatibility of the historical baseline with different levels of green-power surplus and demonstrate how the same statistical-physics construction can estimate any downstream metric expressible through arbitrary functions of generalized moments of the baseline observables. In the absence of more detailed knowledge about the processes forming the historical baseline, large-scale universality, whenever many unknown influences on collective phenomena become negligible, unambiguously offers a principled route to a self-contained ex-ante impact assessment.

papers.title: Sharp Last-Iterate Bounds for the Stochastic subGradient Method
papers.summary: We determine the worst-case expected optimization error of the last iterate of constant-stepsize projected Stochastic subGradient Method on convex Lipschitz objectives. The upper and lower bounds match up to universal constants for every stepsize, horizon, dimension, and conditional noise moment of order $p\in[1,\infty]$. With bounded noise and a fixed positive bound on the initial distance to a minimizer, the best constant stepsize gives worst-case error after $n$ iterates of order $1/\sqrt n$ on the line and $\sqrt{\log n/(n\log\log n)}$ in every fixed dimension at least two.

papers.title: ESSI: Computationally Efficient Semantic Search for Sparse Autoencoder Concepts
papers.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose diffusion model activations into interpretable features, but steering a model with them requires identifying which features map to a given semantic concept, if any. Existing methods for this concept to feature task are expensive, relying on grid searches or repeated passes through the frozen UNet. We propose Efficient Semantic Sparse Identification (ESSI). Using segmentation masks to label SDXL activations as concept or non-concept, ESSI ranks SAE features and binary-searches for the smallest set on which a linear classifier still separates positive from negative samples while not falling below a performance threshold, then reuses that classifier to calibrate the steering strength. We evaluate the same selected features on both concept insertion and object unlearning. Compared with prior work, ESSI is as cheap or cheaper, and performs well on both insertion and removal.
