papers.title: Autonomous Parameter Surgery: How LLMs Implant Selective Backdoors into Language Models
papers.summary: Neural network weights are usually treated as opaque artifacts of gradient descent. Recent work on weight space programming, however, suggests that large language models can inspect and rewrite another network's parameters directly. In this paper, we ask whether a general language model can turn a natural language backdoor specification into persistent, selective weight edits on its own, without gradient training, layer hints, external corpora, or a prescribed editing formula. Using DeepSeek Flash at low reasoning effort inside a restricted workspace that blocks local CPU simulation, we test three open models (Qwen3.5-0.8B, Llama-3.2-1B, SmolLM3-3B) across two review domains (IMDb and Yelp; 18 independent sessions). Evaluated in fresh processes with the editor removed, the modified checkpoints reach 99.2% mean attack success on the editing domain and 97.6% transfer success on the unseen domain, while preserving clean accuracy, low control drift, and general capabilities within 1.7 points of the base models. Our traces show that the model converges on edits in the final layer in 17 of 18 runs and discovers both dense rank-one orthogonalization and single neuron weight surgery at an average cost of \$1.74 per run.

papers.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
papers.summary: Reward-independent representations enable reinforcement learning agents to reuse knowledge across tasks, but limited representation capacity raises three fundamental questions: what statistical dependence should these representations capture, which components of that dependence should be retained for policy improvement, and how does discarding the remaining components affect decision-making? We address these questions through canonical dependence analysis. For a reference policy, we construct an action-centered, positive-lag canonical dependence matrix (CDM) that isolates the additional predictive contribution of the current action beyond the current state. Its singular value decomposition yields Spectral Universal Advantage Features (SUAF), paired features that recover delayed advantage through linear reward projections. We show that the spectrum quantifies mutual information between current action and future state-action visitation conditioned on current state and determines reward specific approximation errors. Retaining the leading modes gives optimal rank-constrained approximations under both isotropic average-case and reward-uniform minimax criteria. Separating the immediate reward contrast also avoids the spectral floor arising from direct compression of the full advantage operator. To learn SUAF from reward-free data, we develop an action-centered Soft-HGR objective with bidirectional temporal-difference estimation. We further connect spectral approximation errors to sufficient conditions for policy improvement. Finite-state experiments validate the spectral predictions and feature-learning method, while zero-shot evaluations on discrete tasks and continuous-control benchmarks demonstrate the utility of the learned representations across rewards.

papers.title: Augmentation of cardiovascular flow measurements with generative diffusion models
papers.summary: Cardiovascular imaging offers several ways to measure blood flow, but each provides an incomplete, resolution-limited, or noisy view of the underlying dynamics. Reconstructing the missing information is inherently ambiguous because several flow fields may be compatible with the same observation. Here, we investigate generative diffusion models as tools for cardiovascular-flow generation and reconstruction using a fully controlled state-of-the-art dataset from a digital twin of a healthy human left heart. First, we show how unconditional samples reproduce the changing anatomy and the highly fluctuating statistical properties of the flow throughout the cardiac cycle. Second, we test the conditional inference of our generative model by reconstructing an entire 2D planar section of geometry and flow configurations from a limited portion. Repeated reconstructions allow us to represent a range of plausible completions, going beyond a single deterministic estimate, while their mean retains the principal features of the reference flow. Comparison with a Gaussian process regression baseline on the same reduced domain highlights the main advantage of diffusion models: their reconstructed ensembles capture a broader range of velocity and gradient fluctuations, better encompassing ground-truth features that the baseline distributions can miss. Our results provide a quantitative proof of concept for probabilistic reconstruction of incomplete cardiovascular-flow measurements and demonstrate the potential for groundbreaking applications to the augmentation of in-vivo cardiovascular imaging data.

papers.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization. We investigate how VLMs can learn transferable 3D representations directly from calibrated binocular observations. To this end, we introduce StereoVLM, the first geometry-aware binocular VLM for metric 3D spatial reasoning. StereoVLM follows a hierarchical learning paradigm spanning from cross-view correspondence and disparity estimation to calibration-conditioned metric depth perception and semantic spatial reasoning. We further find that disparity supervision generalizes substantially better than direct binocular depth supervision on unseen environments. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Stereo3D-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark across three levels, from point-level geometry to object-level spatial reasoning. StereoVLM-8B achieves 95.17% depth accuracy ($δ_1$) and a 66.98 average object-level score on Stereo3D-Bench. Intervention results further indicate that the model's performance on Stereo3D-Bench benefits from valid cross-view geometry and cannot be explained solely by additional visual tokens or semantic priors. Hierarchical geometric supervision also yields average gains of 3.54 points across five spatial benchmarks and 4.3 percentage points in RoboCasa manipulation success.

papers.title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
papers.summary: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law. We also prove that this ensemble can be written as a sum of asymptotically free random density operators, leading to an alternative proof of the convergence of the spectral distribution. Finally, we compute the asymptotic expansion of the average entanglement entropy.

papers.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
papers.summary: Detecting individual instances is crucial for many segmentation problems. However, expert instance annotations are often unavailable, so instances are approximated heuristically (e.g., as connected components of semantic maps), which can merge touching objects or split fragmented ones. Even when expert annotations exist, expert disagreement or structural delineation biases can yield split or merged reference instances, corresponding to over- or under-segmentation, respectively. Panoptic Quality (PQ) and related metrics capture both segmentation and detection quality while weighting all instances equally, regardless of size. Yet when the references are biased, these metrics can neither detect split or merged instances nor distinguish valid from invalid overor under-segmentation. We present Star Panoptic Quality (StarPQ), a novel evaluation ramework, which closes this gap in two steps: First, we construct a so-called star forest in the bipartite graph whose clean, merge, and split stars isolate different failure modes. Second, we calculate the final metric by individually weighting each failure mode, allowing practitioners to account for instance delineation biases. Across various experiments, we demonstrate that StarPQ not only enables targeted penalization or eniency towards specific failure modes, but also serves as a diagnostic tool to reveal their prevalence.

papers.title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
papers.summary: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. Tracking this quantity across public checkpoints of Pythia, OLMo, and Amber yields three findings. First, write-relative connected coordination strengthens from its initialization or earliest-checkpoint baseline as pretraining proceeds, across all measured interaction orders. Second, these connected components are behaviorally consequential under direct intervention: deleting them damages perplexity more than deleting a norm-matched random direction at the same site in all 35 measured model-order cells. Third, pairwise representation similarity is consistently negatively correlated with pairwise connected coordination across seven models, yet the two signals are not interchangeable: similarity- and coordination-based block-removal criteria often agree in Pythia but diverge on Amber. Together, these results suggest that architectural depth provides the opportunity for sequential computation, while pretraining progressively organizes cross-layer dependencies within that depth.

papers.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
papers.summary: Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties. We propose interpretable embeddings built from decision columns: each column stores a decision model's calibrated answer to a natural-language question, with outcomes yes, no, or not stated. A record's embedding is its answers across an ordered set of questions. Similarity decomposes exactly into per-question contributions, and new questions add coordinates without altering existing ones. On public product benchmarks, question-space retrieval matches dense candidate generation statistically in a retrieve-then-verify entity matcher, while providing exact explanations for accepted matches. Questions derived from retrieval failures triple mean reciprocal rank without re-encoding prior answers. For search, inferring the attributes of a suitable result outperforms encoding only the literal request, and combining question-space and dense scores improves retrieval, though not at our prespecified confidence threshold. A single small neural network predicts the full interpretable vector from an existing dense embedding, enabling corpus backfilling from a few thousand labeled rows at roughly 1/200 the cost. We position interpretable embeddings as a complementary, readable retrieval channel for explaining matches, filtering on attributes, and extending indexes as failures expose missing facts.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 7 figures, including appendices. Evaluations on WDC Products and STaRK-Amazon

papers.title: Metadata-Private Voice Communication over Tor using Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation
papers.summary: Encrypted voice communication systems commonly protect call content but expose significant metadata, including the network identities of both parties, call timing, and traffic patterns. Simultaneously, advances in quantum computing threaten the asymmetric primitives underlying conventional key exchange, creating a harvest-now, decrypt-later risk for long-lived sensitive communications. Existing systems address at most one of these concerns: secure VoIP applications such as Signal and Wire rely on centralized infrastructure and classical cryptography, while anonymous communication tools built on the Tor network support only text messaging and lack post-quantum key encapsulation. This paper presents SAPEC (Secure Anonymous Peer Exchange Communicator), a peer-to-peer voice communication system that simultaneously addresses anonymity, decentralization, and quantum resistance. SAPEC routes all traffic exclusively through Tor hidden services, concealing the IP addresses of both parties, and augments the standard TLS handshake with a custom protocol layer that performs ML-KEM-1024 key establishment, a settle on AES-256 symmetrical keys and mutual Dilithium identity verification before any audio is transmitted. All audio is subsequently encrypted under AES-256. A removable Crypto Ignition Key prevents identity key material from being stored on the device. Empirical evaluation across 45 independently circuit-rebuilt test runs yielded a median one-way audio delay of 355 milliseconds and a median connection setup time of 7.61 seconds on same-region Tor circuits, demonstrating that interactive voice communication over onion routing is practically achievable.
papers.comment: 8 Pages, 5 Figures, Project was also presented in the german youth science competition Jugend Forscht under the name SAPEC - Secure Anonymous Peer Exchange Communicator

papers.title: AnimalFarm: Auditing the Generation and Detection of Hateful Images Featuring Anthropomorphic Characters
papers.summary: Anthropomorphic non-human characters have long been used to convey hateful messages targeting human groups, from Nazi-era propaganda to recent AI-generated imagery on social media. However, the safety risks posed by such imagery remain largely unexplored. We thus conduct the first systematic study of hateful image generation and detection involving anthropomorphic non-human characters. We construct a benchmark from conservatively screened source scenes, covering five character types and three image generation tasks: text-to-image generation, image editing, and conversational image generation. Across 14,250 scheduled queries, image generation systems produce images for 92.1\% of queries, of which 95.9\% contain hateful content. We further collect 4,370 hateful images and evaluate five popular hateful-content detectors. Even the strongest detector, GPT-5.5, identifies only 73.9\% of hateful images, while most detect fewer than 58\%. Our analysis reveals that existing detectors often misclassify hateful images as benign when their main subjects are non-human characters. We explore two effective mitigation approaches: a training-free pipeline that maps non-human characters back to human representations before classification and a detector fine-tuned for this type of hateful content. These approaches achieve F1 scores of 0.962 and 0.979, respectively. Our findings expose significant safety gaps in both image generation and hateful-content detection. Disclaimer: This paper contains hateful text and imagery.

papers.title: Data-Adaptive Entropy-Based Moment Reduction for Vlasov-Poisson-Dougherty Dynamics
papers.summary: We develop a data-adaptive entropy-based moment method for the Vlasov-Poisson-Dougherty system with self-consistent temperature. A positive exponential representation augments the physical moments with data-adapted velocity functions. The collision guarantees are independent of basis construction: for every fixed basis satisfying the stated rank condition, the reduced collision step is uniquely solvable, positive, locally conservative and entropy-dissipative. These guarantees persist under a positive empirical cubature method (ECM), enabling structure-preserving collision hyper-reduction. We construct the basis by proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), fit it with a neural network and post-train it through the reduced dynamics. In two-stream relaxation, sustained heating and drive switching, one fixed post-trained basis with thirteen variables per cell attains space-time distribution errors below 0.25% against same-grid full-order solutions. Post-training lowers this error relative to the neural fit in all three tests and to POD in the two driven tests. With full-grid MUSCL retained, matched drive-switching timings give 1.36-2.89-fold online speedups over the full-order solver using 128-1024 velocity nodes.

papers.title: Non autonomous problems with nearly linear growth and Orlicz-Sobolev coefficients
papers.summary: We establish the local Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers of non autonomous integral functionals of the form \[ \mathcal{F}(u, Ω) = \int_ΩF(x, Du)\, {\mathrm d}x, \] where $Ω$ is a bounded open set of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 2$ and the energy density $F(x,ξ)$ satisfies nearly linear growth conditions with respect to the gradient variable. The main novelty of this work lies in the identification of a suitable quantitative balance between the logarithmic degeneration of the ellipticity and an Orlicz-Sobolev regularity of the partial map $x\to {F(x,ξ)}$ that is sufficient to obtain the Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers.

papers.title: Growth of subsolutions to fully nonlinear equations in halfspaces II
papers.summary: We establish sharp lower growth estimates for subsolutions of fully nonlinear elliptic equations in half-spaces, allowing source terms that depend explicitly on the solution. The estimates capture both growth at infinity and blow-up at a finite distance from the boundary. Our approach extends the ODE-based method introduced in [J. Differential Equations 320 (2022), 143--173].

papers.title: QuantStream3D: Geometry-Aligned Low-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Streaming Visual Geometry Transformers
papers.summary: Streaming visual geometry transformers retain historical key-value (KV) states as cross-view geometric memory, but growing caches constrain long-sequence inference. We systematically characterize KV quantization in streaming geometry and uncover two linked challenges: Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch. Quantization sensitivity varies across precision choices and cache locations, while perturbed retrieval changes geometry-head inputs and propagates through subsequent predictions and KV writes. Guided by these findings, we propose QuantStream3D, to our knowledge the first dedicated KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers. Geometry-Guided Mixed-Precision KV Quantization protects sensitive cross-view evidence, while Geometry-Aligned Quantization-Aware Distillation jointly adapts transformer blocks and geometry heads on student-generated quantized history. Across five benchmarks and two backbones, QuantStream3D achieves near-lossless geometric accuracy in most settings with predominantly 2-bit KV caches, and many configurations surpass unquantized inference. Compared with LLM-oriented KV quantizers, it reduces TUM absolute trajectory error and NeuralRGBD completeness error by up to 57.4% and 69.7%, respectively. Integration with existing native cache-pruning methods further pushes compression while improving reconstruction quality on NeuralRGBD. Our optimized StreamVGGT backend achieves $5.05\times$ physical KV compression and 23.1% lower latency at batch size one. Under a fixed memory budget on the same GPU, it supports $5.4\times$ the maximum batch size and up to $1.67\times$ the peak throughput of unquantized inference. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
papers.summary: Electronic health records (EHRs) contain rich health information for uncovering latent patient representations and clinically meaningful subgroups. Learning from EHR data across institutions is valuable because representations learned at a single site may reflect local data patterns and lack generalizability, yet pooling patient-level records across institutions is often impractical because of privacy constraints and communication costs. We propose a communication-efficient, non-iterative federated spectral method for learning shared latent representation components from multi-institutional EHRs, in which each institution shares aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary while keeping patient-level records local. A central server aggregates these summaries with the pooled marginal frequencies to recover both the shared low-rank structure and the canonical row-normalization direction required for interpretable representation recovery. We prove row-wise recovery guarantees and error bounds, with a leading federated variance term matching a corresponding lower bound under explicit regularity conditions. Simulations show that our method closely matches pooled analysis in estimating latent representation components, improves as more sites contribute summaries, and outperforms single-site and existing federated benchmarks across a range of data settings. Applied to real-world multi-facility EHR data for stroke patients, the method learns interpretable patient representations that highlight clinically distinct subgroups and could help inform subgroup-specific care.
papers.comment: 10 pages of main text (76 pages including references and appendices). Accepted for presentation at NeurIPS 2026

papers.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
papers.summary: Sustaining user experience (UX) quality in large-scale web search requires scalable evaluation. Traditional surveys are slow and bottleneck rapid A/B testing, while automated metrics often lack the granularity to diagnose visual-spatial UX anomalies. To address this, we introduce the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, a novel industrial architecture for automated UX attribution. Tier 1 (Macro System) acts as a scalable user sentiment regression detector, utilizing a fine-tuned encoder-decoder LLM (based on Gemini XS) on telemetry features. Through multi-task regularization and contextual feature engineering, this tier achieves a +9.8% PR-AUC gain on over 500,000 held-out records, matching baseline recall on all validated regressions with $\sim$20% relative precision gain among the 12 held-out experiments. In production, it reduces measurement latency from weeks to hours and cuts survey overhead by over 40%. Tier 2 (Micro System) provides granular diagnostics by employing a Multimodal LLM (Gemini 3.0 Pro) to natively assess visual renderings and spatial layout of web result blocks, quantifying "User Toil" as the estimated effort required to reach a satisfactory result. Enhanced by RL-based automated prompt optimization and an AI judge for win/loss patterns, the MLLM yields a $>$6.5% F1 score improvement, offering deep insights into content quality and layout friction. Ultimately, this framework enables scalable, accurate, and diagnostic UX attribution, processing O(100k) live experiment queries daily.

papers.title: An early interaction between the Sagittarius dwarf and the Milky Way I: Fossil signatures in the phase-space structure of the disc
papers.summary: Several independent lines of evidence point to an early encounter between the Milky Way and the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy $5$-$7$ Gyr ago. We present four controlled $N$-body+hydro simulations, one of an isolated host galaxy and three of a single interaction between a Milky-Way-like host and a Sagittarius-like satellite on an unbound polar orbit. Relative to the fiducial satellite (with total mass $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$), one run increases the satellite's mass by a factor of $1.5$ and another its crossing speed by a factor of $1.4$, giving pericentric speeds of $466$-$634$ km s$^{-1}$ at pericentric radii of $R\simeq15$-$18$ kpc. Comparing the present-day, phase-space structure in radial bins by age of newly-formed thin-disc stars across the runs, we find that stars that existed at the time of the passage are thickened by up to $\sim37$ per cent in mass-enclosed height and heated by up to $\sim5$ km s$^{-1}$ in vertical velocity dispersion relative to the control, while stars formed after the passage are unaffected. The heating signature is also evident when comparing the age-vertical velocity dispersion relation against a heating relation with a power law of $0.38$, obtained by fitting the isolated host. A single, disc crossing from an early interaction thus suffices to leave lasting, datable fossils in the age-resolved vertical structure of a galactic disc. The fiducial run's dispersion jump of $\sim4$ km s$^{-1}$ matches best with that observed in the outer low-$α$ disc of the Milky Way (Das et al. 2024), corresponding to a perturber mass of $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$, with a velocity of $466$ km s$^{-1}$ at a pericentric radius of $16.7$ kpc, though the inversion from jump amplitude to perturber mass is good only to a factor of $\sim1.5$.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to MNRAS

papers.title: Extreme Value Inference with Measurement Error: Application to Earthquake Magnitudes
papers.summary: Extreme value analyses typically assume that observations are measured without error, yet many environmental measurements are subject to different levels of observational uncertainty depending on the context. Ignoring such measurement error can distort inference on the tail behaviour. In this paper, we focus on peaks-over-threshold models, where exceedances above a high threshold are typically modelled using the generalised Pareto distribution (GPD). We develop a statistical framework for extreme value inference when observations are noisy measurements of an underlying true variable. Measurement error introduces a particular challenge in threshold-based extreme value analysis, as latent exceedances may be observed below the threshold, while latent non-exceedances may be observed above it. To address this problem, we represent the latent distribution using a hybrid body--tail specification, combining a flexible nonparametric body with a GPD tail. We develop a computationally efficient partially censored likelihood inference approach for data of this structure. The framework allows the measurement error scale and the GPD parameters to depend on covariates. Simulation studies demonstrate biases on the tail inference from ignoring measurement error and that our approach overcomes such impacts. The methodology is motivated by, and illustrated using, the catalogue of induced earthquake magnitudes from the Groningen, Netherlands, one of the largest gas fields in the world.

papers.title: Optimised 8th-Order Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Quantum Simulation
papers.summary: Simulating quantum dynamics in many-body systems is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. Product formulas are a natural choice for this task, since they map directly onto quantum gates, and increasing their order $n$ could lead to reduced gate depths, provided the parameters are chosen efficiently. So far, schemes beyond $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order have only been built as compositions of second-order schemes, while more general product formulas are known only up to $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. In this work, we extend our optimisation framework to order $n = 8$, and find both more efficient compositions and the first $8^{\textrm{th}}$ order general schemes. Our formulas improve on the theoretical efficiency of the state-of-the-art schemes by Morales et al and we recommend two schemes explicitly. In simulations of the Heisenberg XZ chain one of our recommended schemes always outperforms those by Morales et al, though it is not always the same scheme that performs best. More generally, we observe that for Hamiltonians split into many non-commuting operators the uniformity of a Trotter decomposition becomes the main indicator of a scheme's performance. To assess the schemes' use on quantum hardware, we simulate noisy circuits with our new Qiskit plugin qiskit-omelyan. At current noise levels, the Leapfrog scheme remains the best choice, but as noise rates decrease toward fault tolerance, our recommended schemes become competitive.

papers.title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?
papers.summary: Coding agents increasingly implement rules written by domain experts, and bugs in such code are silent: it runs and returns a plausible answer. We introduce TEA-Bench-BR, a benchmark built on the Brazilian pathway for early autism (TEA) screening: three fictitious instruments with the structure of real ones, a multi-professional referral flow, and export to FHIR R4 with the national RNDS profiles, all specified in Portuguese. A generator samples each task's parameters (144 tasks, 6,798 hidden cases), and the hidden cases kill all 1,955 non-equivalent mutants of the reference. With Gemma 4 as the agent, the 12B solves 38.0% of single-instrument tasks and none at the FHIR level; the 31B solves 77.8%, 85.2% and 78.7% at levels 1 to 3 and passes over 99% of the hidden cases, its remaining failures mostly in input validation rather than clinical decisions. With the same tasks in English, the 31B solves 57.4% at level 3, as its code validates an identifier less often; the 12B's, more often. The 12B misses 10.10% of the cases that call for referral; the 31B, 0.02%. A contamination probe on a modified PHQ-9 finds no error that follows the original rules.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to the Google Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track (Kaggle, November 2026). Benchmark, code and results: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24143388

papers.title: FairITR: Fairness-Aware Learning of Multicategory Individualized Treatment Rules
papers.summary: Individualized treatment rules (ITRs) recommend treatment decisions based on individual characteristics and can improve treatment outcomes beyond traditional one-size-fits-all strategies. However, similar to other commonly used algorithmic decision-making methods, ITRs without considering model fairness may result in unfair decisions across groups defined by sensitive attributes, such as race or gender. Although extensive methods have been developed for ITR estimation, most focus solely on optimizing treatment outcomes, while research on fairness-aware ITRs remains limited. Moreover, the practical scenario of multicategory treatments is rarely considered in existing fair ITR studies. To address these gaps, we introduce a fairness notion for multicategory ITRs that requires treatment decisions to be independent of sensitive attributes, and then formulate the corresponding problem of estimating fair ITRs. To solve this problem, we further propose FairITR, a fairness-aware learning framework that jointly optimizes treatment outcomes and fairness. FairITR builds on angle-based classification for multicategory ITR learning and integrates adversarial learning with covariance-based regularization to mitigate unfairness in treatment decisions. A theoretical justification for the fairness properties induced by the adversarial debiasing mechanism is also provided. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that FairITR substantially reduces unfairness in ITRs while maintaining competitive treatment values relative to existing baselines.

papers.title: Multi-scale dynamic latent space models improve inference for a social predator
papers.summary: Social networks are dynamic in nature. Examining changes in dynamic networks provides insights into the drivers and consequences of social interactions. Dynamic latent space models (DLSMs) quantify social tie strength through a distance measure between latent positions in an unobservable, low-dimensional space. Conditional on the latent positions, ties are assumed independent, and temporal dynamics are introduced through autocorrelated trajectories. These trajectories are typically modeled as random walks; however, random walks lack the mechanism to characterize network clustering, where individuals from the same group tend to form stronger ties than those across groups. Therefore, we extend the framework of DLSM to distinguish within-group dynamics from between-group dynamics. Our approach employs coupled movement models operating at two scales in the latent space to encode community structure using autoregressive processes with attraction. Through simulation studies, we show that when cluster separation is high, our framework improves coverage of linear predictors and enhances overall model fit relative to a naive DLSM. When cluster separation is moderate, performance remains comparable to that of the naive approach. In addition, our method demonstrates empirical computational advantages over the naive DLSM, with potential for further efficiency gains. We apply our framework to a case study of gray wolf (Canis lupus) interactions over three decades in Yellowstone National Park, where it provides improved model performance and novel insights into wolf social dynamics.

papers.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
papers.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by preparing candidate continuations before the target model generates them. Its efficiency depends on how well limited drafting computation anticipates the path the target will actually follow. Anticipating this path involves two sources of uncertainty: the target model's predictions and the randomness of sampling. Yet the former requires a target-model forward pass, while the latter can be fixed before drafting. Building on this observation, we introduce DICE (Draw-Informed Candidate Selection), which pre-samples and synchronizes verification randomness across drafting and verification. By combining these known draws with predictions from an existing drafter, DICE allocates computation toward continuations more likely to be used in the current sampling run. This principle guides node selection throughout draft-tree construction and extends to asynchronous prefetching, where DICE predicts which next-round drafts to prepare. Without additional drafter training or changes to the target sampling distribution, DICE achieves state-of-the-art decoding throughput across diverse settings, with speedups of up to 24.6pp over strong baselines.

papers.title: A TESS Search for Optical Variability in Intermediate-mass Black Hole Candidates
papers.summary: Optical variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) probes accretion onto black holes. We study the optical variability of AGNs in the mass range of intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs, $10^{2-6}\,M_\odot$), whose expected variability damping timescales are of order days. We use the high-cadence photometry of the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to search for optical variability within its individual 28-day sectors. By applying the Quaver light-curve reduction pipeline and designing artifact-aware variability metrics, we identify 3 sources with high-confidence variability and 17 sources with medium-confidence variability. Fitting damped random walk (DRW) models reveals a tentative timescale-mass correlation in a small, metric-selected subset, but not in the full sample. ZTF difference-image aperture photometry reveals long-term fractional variability of 1.8-7.4% in the high-confidence sources, while most medium-confidence sources have variability below 1%. This study demonstrates that the dense cadence and repeated full-sky observations of TESS are valuable for detecting IMBH optical variability, while also being limited by its instrumental artifacts and relatively shallow field.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ApJ

papers.title: Renormalized Entropy from Symmetries: Simplicity Bias and Neural Heat Death
papers.summary: Neural networks have parameter symmetries: parameter transformations that do not affect the represented function. How do these symmetries affect the functions that neural networks ultimately learn? We study the implicit bias arising from these symmetries by calculating the equilibrium distribution over represented functions under Langevin dynamics with Gaussian regularization. To isolate the effect of symmetries on this distribution, we study the limit in which the strength of the regularization is taken to zero. In certain cases, we show that the zero-regularization and infinite-time limits commute. In the low temperature limit, we recover known effective regularizations. At positive temperature, a renormalization procedure allows us to derive a novel entropy which predicts symmetry-induced preference for certain functions. For linear networks, we obtain explicit entropy terms that favor singular and low-rank functions. For networks with homogeneous activations, we find entropy terms that favor inactive neurons, which can lead to neural "heat death" in which equilibrium mass concentrates on networks with vanishing output. We interpret these results through the neural tangent kernel, as a simplicity bias selecting for functions that vary slowly under variations in the parameters.

papers.title: Spatial model of neurogliovascular unit: arachidonic acid can control the stability
papers.summary: Arachidonic acid metabolites can have both vasoconstrictor and vasodilator effects, thereby influencing neuronal activity. In this work, to analyze possible patterns of activity of nervous tissue in response to changes in the metabolic profile, a mathematical model of a spatially distributed system of connected neurogliovascular units was developed. We simulate the influence of arachidonic acid metabolites on the dynamics of the neurogliovascular unit during cortical spreading depression in order to determine the ways in which astrocytic activity influences the spatiotemporal characteristics of the propagating cortical depression wave. It is assumed that in the future the results of the theoretical study can be used to find ways to remove nervous tissue from pathological conditions that occur in epilepsy, migraines and a number of neurodegenerative diseases, including those associated with the occurrence of cortical depression waves.
papers.journal: D. V. Verveyko, A. Y. Verisokin and P. O. Lukin. Spatial model of neurogliovascular unit: arachidonic acid can control the stability. Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications, 2024, pp. 254-257

papers.title: Recurrent sets and Lyapunov functions: from topological dynamics to weak KAM theory
papers.summary: The aim of this survey is to clarify the intimate relations between Lyapunov functions and chain recurrent sets. The study of this subject comes from a seminal paper by Conley and has had recent advances by the so-called Weak KAM Theory for homeomorphisms. We provide a survey of the state of the art, presenting recent improvements and connections with the stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, in order to illustrate the distinctions between recurrent sets in a non-trivial case as well as their dependence on a parameter, we discuss a compartmental model from mathematical epidemiology and a fast-slow version of a prey-predator model with Allee effect.

papers.title: The Science and Mythology of Sports Rankings: Evaluating the methods, assumptions, and attributes used to rank NCAA teams
papers.summary: Selecting a sports-ranking system is not a purely mathematical decision. It also requires agreement about what the ranking should mean and what institutional purpose it should serve. This paper distinguishes four related but different tasks in sports ranking: prediction, retrospective evaluation, championship selection, and seeding; compares the governing philosophies of major ranking families; and identifies recurring errors in ranking debates. A descriptive comparison of nine NCAA Division I sport settings illustrates how schedule density, scoring environment, cross-conference connectivity, head-to-head meetings, and common-opponent availability vary from sport to sport. The central premise is that no ranking methodology is value-free. Every system reflects choices about evidence, competitive merit, and which tradeoffs are acceptable. The paper therefore offers a structured, multi-objective framework for evaluating ranking systems according to their intended purpose/goal rather than naming one universally superior method. Its principal contribution is to make the philosophical and institutional assumptions behind ranking decisions explicit, comparable, and testable.

papers.title: FR3-Band Capacitive-Piezoelectric Thin-Film LN Resonator for Heterogeneous Integration
papers.summary: This letter presents a capacitively coupled piezoelectric lateral-field-excited bulk acoustic wave resonator (XBAR) in single-crystal lithium niobate (LN) for frequency range 3 (FR3, 7.125-24.25 GHz). We develop a platform that simultaneously maintains high electromechanical efficiency (\(k_t^2\)) and quality factor (\(Q\)) while alleviating challenges associated with parasitic galvanic interconnections and is fit for heterogeneous integration above integrated circuits. A 100 nm air gap excites the second-order symmetric Lamb wave (S2) mode in a 500 nm thick periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) LN from a fused silica substrate via flip-chip bonding, yielding a resonance frequency (\(f_s\)) of 7.16 GHz with an extracted \(k_t^2\) of 12.25\% and \(Q\) of 100, facilitating a high \(Q\cdot k_t^2\cdot f_s\) product of 87.71. The results demonstrate strong piezoelectric transduction through a nanoscale air gap, supporting further development of the platform for heterogeneous integration of compact, low-loss microwave components.

papers.title: Thermo-electric Response Bound on Fluctuations in Coherent Transport
papers.summary: We establish an accessible lower bound on current noise in coherent electron transport, expressed in terms of responses to reservoir temperatures and chemical potentials. Derived within the Floquet-Nambu scattering formalism using a Cramér-Rao-type inequality, it holds for arbitrary linear combinations of charge and heat currents in normal terminals, including those of hybrid superconducting systems, under static or periodic driving. The bound is tight in experimentally relevant regimes, notably in quantum point contacts with static or oscillating voltages and normal-superconductor junctions, often providing stronger constraints than thermodynamic uncertainty relations. It can be evaluated via experimentally accessible response coefficients, without inferring entropy production or dynamical activity, and provides useful constraints on the precision of nanoscale thermal and quantum devices.

papers.title: Soft-photon resummation for low-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders
papers.summary: We present resummed predictions for $e^+e^- \to μ^+μ^-(γ)$ and $π^+π^-(γ)$ in the multi-photon soft limit, matched to exact NLO. The resummation is performed within the Yennie-Frautschi-Suura framework at the amplitude level. The initial and final-state contributions are included coherently, and NLO accuracy with finite electron, muon and pion masses is achieved. We present our calculation, its implementation in a fast Fortran Monte Carlo integrator, and compare our predictions with the generators BabaYaga, KKMC, Phokhara and McMule, in scenarios inspired by the energy-scan (CMD) and radiative-return (KLOE, BES III, B factories) experiments. We find agreement with BabaYaga, which includes higher-order corrections through a parton shower, at the per-mille level in the cross-sections, and differences of up to two percent with the soft-photon resummation of KKMC. This work represents an important step towards the validation of Monte Carlo generators for low-energy experiments, and will be released in the upcoming new version of Phokhara.

papers.title: Cobham theorem for expansive bases in orders of number fields
papers.summary: We prove a Cobham theorem for bases $α,β$ in the ring of integers $R$ of a number field $K$ of degree $d\ge 2$, the bases being expansive, that is, of absolute value greater than $1$ at every archimedean place. The two required conditions are $\mathbb Q(α^r,β^s)=K$ and $α^r R\neβ^s R$ for all $r,s\ge 1$. Under these conditions, a function from $R$ to a finite alphabet is automatic in both bases if and only if it is eventually periodic, that is, if it agrees, outside a finite set, with a function periodic for a subgroup of $R$ of rank $d$. Both conditions are necessary: if either fails, some subset of $R$ is automatic in both bases without being eventually periodic. The proof distinguishes bases with different and with equal prime-ideal supports, using recognisability of constant-shape substitutions and comparisons of exact affine symmetries. The result extends to arbitrary orders, to lattices stable under the bases, and to suitable pairs of commuting expansive integer matrices.

papers.title: Interpretable Tissue Architecture Complements Pathology Foundation Models
papers.summary: Tissue architecture provides important information for histopathological assessment, yet its complementary predictive value alongside pathology foundation-model representations remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates whether interpretable measurements of cellular and multicellular tissue organization provide additional predictive information beyond learned representations. We introduce a 139-dimensional cellular-to-community representation comprising nine feature groups characterizing nuclear morphology, cellular composition, spatial connectivity, community organization, and cell-cell interactions. Their predictive contributions are systematically evaluated independently and through feature-level fusion with CTransPath and PLIP embeddings using multiple-instance learning (MIL). On the BCNB dataset, estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) classification is evaluated across four MIL architectures using five-fold patient-disjoint cross-validation. Selected CTransPath fusion configurations achieved mean ROC-AUC values of 0.9144 (ER) and 0.8360 (PR), while PLIP fusion achieved 0.8791 and 0.8015, respectively. Patient-level analyses identified ER-associated differences in nuclear morphology, graph connectivity, cellular communities, and cell-cell interactions. On LungHist700, selected fusion configurations achieved higher mean ROC-AUC across four classification tasks, including adenocarcinoma versus squamous cell carcinoma (0.7967 versus 0.7137 for CTransPath alone). Overall, these findings suggest that interpretable tissue-architecture descriptors can complement foundation-model representations while providing measurable insights into histopathological organization.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to Biomedical Signal Processing and Control

papers.title: Study of two-photon femtoscopic correlations in Ag+Ag collisions at $\mathbf{\sqrt{s_{NN}}}$ = 2.55 GeV with HADES
papers.summary: Two-photon correlations can provide unique femtoscopic information, complementing those obtained with charged particles. They also allow to estimate the direct photon yield in the low $p_{T}$ region. We present experimental results on $γ-γ$ correlations in Ag+Ag collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.55 GeV, collected by the HADES experiment. Photons were measured using an electromagnetic calorimeter (ECAL) and two-photon correlations were determined as one-dimen-sional functions $CF(q_{inv})$. We discuss the observed structures, along with their plausible origin. Finally, we estimate an upper limit for the correlation strength of direct photons for two confidence levels, resulting in values of the order $10^{-4}-10^{-3}$ .

papers.title: On the chromatic splitting conjecture in coheight $1$
papers.summary: This article confirms predictions made by Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture in stable homotopy theory. A consequence of our main theorem is that a certain map of $K(h-1)$-local $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings $\mathbb{S}_{K(h-1)}^{B\mathbb{Z}}\to L_{K(h-1)}\mathbb{S}_{K(h)}$ admits a retract, so long as $p-1$ does not divide $h-1$. If $h=2$ and $p$ is odd, we show this map is an isomorphism. We use methods from the theory of $p$-divisible groups and $p$-adic geometry. Along the way we prove an entirely new kind of "two-tower isomorphism," in analogy with Faltings' isomorphism between the Lubin--Tate and Drinfeld towers, which parametrizes $p$-divisible groups over characteristic $p$ perfectoid spaces with fixed generic fiber in terms of negative Banach--Colmez spaces. Using the two-tower isomorphism, we gain control over the continuous cohomology of the Morava stabilizer group $\mathbb{G}_h$ with coefficients in $π_*L_{K(h-1)}E_h$. To study the continuous action of $\mathbb{G}_h$ on $L_{K(h-1)} E_h$, it was necessary to develop the theory of solid Lubin--Tate spectra. Adapting Lurie's constructions, we attach a solid Lubin--Tate spectrum to $p$-divisible groups over a broad class of solid rings in characteristic $p$.

papers.title: On the interplay between the anisotropy and the regularity of the coefficients in non autonomous problems
papers.summary: We establish the local Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers of non autonomous integral {functionals} of the form \begin{equation*} \label{functional} {\mathcal{F}(z) =} \int_ΩF(x, Dz)\,dx, \end{equation*} where $Ω$ is a bounded open set of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 2$ and the energy density $F(x,ξ)$ satisfies general growth conditions with respect to the gradient variable. The main novelty of this work lies in the identification of a suitable condition on the interplay between the regularity of the partial map $x\to {F(x,ξ)}$ and the ratio of the non uniform ellipticity of the problem that is sufficient to obtain the Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers. Our result extends and unifies those previously known from the literature, including the standard $p-$growth case.

papers.title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
papers.summary: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it relies on, and leaves every number to a deterministic guideline engine. On four public longitudinal CT datasets, LesionAgent tracks more lesions and measures them more accurately than every automatic baseline, and where the same 3D models chained by fixed rules call progression falsely at 33 of 56 follow-ups, it does so twice. On clinical follow-up CTs, it agrees with the radiologists' response at 20 of 23 follow-ups, including every change in response, and without training on DeepLesion, it retrieves more of its lesions than every tracker trained on it (89.0% vs. 87.4%). Its harness, not its LLM, makes the difference: given the same LLM and 3D models but not the harness, Claude Code reaches a detection F1 of 41% and LesionAgent 78%, and an open-weight LLM that can run inside the hospital rises from 6% to 73%. LesionAgent and a napari reading app for any LLM are available at https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/LesionAgent.

papers.title: From Gist to Verbatim: The Controllable Path of One Image Through a Diffusion Prior
papers.summary: Modern generative models are typically studied for their ability to generalize, while memorization is treated as a failure mode. We invert this perspective and ask how a generative model can recall a single datum. We frame memorization as a control problem: a learned conditioning signal steers a frozen diffusion model toward a target image, and we follow the formation of this memory throughout training. Before converging to exact reproduction (verbatim), memory passes through a regime of abstraction: samples preserve the target's semantic content (gist) while remaining diverse in appearance, leaving predictable detail to the generative prior. This semantic organization emerges despite the absence of labels, captions, or any explicit semantic objective. In the abstraction regime, the learned memory approaches ordinary text conditioning and supports editing, one-shot recognition, and retrieval more effectively than in the near-perfect reconstruction regime. These results suggest that memorization can serve as a probe of the relevance structure encoded by a generative model: what must be stored about a datum, what can be reconstructed from prior knowledge, and how learned memories interpolate between reconstructive recall and literal data storage.

papers.title: Quantum Dobrushin comparison and locality of fermionic equilibrium states
papers.summary: We prove a quantum analogue of Dobrushin's comparison theorem for lattice fermions. As in the classical case, it is a tool for proving uniqueness of equilibrium states, decay of correlations, and stability of local expectations under distant perturbations. We apply it to fermions with weak many-body interactions added to a quadratic Hamiltonian, allowing pairing, spatial inhomogeneity and long-range interactions. If the quadratic Hamiltonian is gapped, there is a coupling strength below which the thermal equilibrium (KMS) state is unique at every positive temperature and its correlations decay uniformly in the temperature. Its local expectations converge to those of the unique gapped ground state exponentially fast in the inverse temperature. In the same regime, local perturbations perturb locally in a strong sense (strong LPPL): every equilibrium state of a system with a distant defect is locally close to the equilibrium state without the defect, however strong or extended the defect is. The same holds for finite-volume Gibbs states with arbitrary even boundary terms. Without a gap, uniqueness, decay of correlations and strong LPPL hold at each positive temperature for interactions below a coupling strength that depends on the temperature. At high temperature, they hold for general interactions.

papers.title: On the long-time behaviour and asymptotic geometry of nonlocal aggregation equations with saturating mobility
papers.summary: We investigate a two-dimensional nonlocal conservation law with a saturating Lipschitz mobility, without assuming concavity of the mobility. For attractive radial potentials, we establish global entropy well-posedness and exact mass confinement. When the interaction potential is quadratic on the active interaction zone of the solution, the nonlocal convolution reduces to an affine drift. This reduction bounds the total path length of the moving barycentre via macroscopic energy dissipation, establishing strong $L^1$ relative compactness of the trajectory through a late-time core-filling approximation that traps the entropic state via $L^1$ contraction, circumventing the imposition of a uniform bounded variation estimate. This compactness, combined with the energy dissipation, forces the entropic trajectory to converge strongly in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ as $t \to \infty$ to a unique stationary binary state. We characterize the geometry of this limit, proving an equivalence with measure-theoretically star-shaped sets. We demonstrate that the nonlocal dynamics admit non-circular stationary equilibria and do not select a unique saturated disk absent radial symmetry on the initial datum. Finally, for entropic stationary binary states of finite perimeter, we exclude essentially bounded measure-theoretic components of the support complement under strict subharmonicity of the interaction potential, and rule out positively separated support components under uniform convexity.

papers.title: World Models for Learning Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
papers.summary: We propose using world models for learning Hamiltonians from measured dynamics of a quantum computer or simulator. Implicitly, the parameters of a Hamiltonian are encoded in how the measured few-body observables evolve. By using a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to perform prediction in latent space, we show that the device Hamiltonian can be efficiently inferred from noisy measurements. We train a spatiotemporal encoder and predictor with approximately $2.7$ million trainable weights using a single objective, to predict the representation of the next window of measurements from the previous one. The network is thereby driven to retain the reproducible dynamics and discard shot noise. We recover the field and coupling maps of a two-dimensional Ising lattice in real and imaginary time, and the disorder map of a one-dimensional Heisenberg chain of $100$ sites. In every settings the encoder achieves lower error than a masked autoencoder and than the same encoder left untrained. It also outperforms the same regression head applied directly to time-averaged observables, by factors of $4.4$ to $30$. We establish latent prediction as a practical self-supervised objective for learning from measurements of quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Beyond Visual Fidelity: Comparing Categorical and Continuous World Models
papers.summary: Visual world models can now generate compelling interactive worlds, but visual realism does not guarantee faithful dynamics. We systematically compare how categorical and continuous prediction shape learned dynamics under both next-token and iterative whole-frame generation. These choices are often bundled in approaches such as autoregressive token models and whole-frame flow matching. We design controlled 2D and 3D environments and evaluate dynamics validity, calibration, and visual quality. In 2D with lossless visual encoding, categorical models achieve higher rollout validity with less training compute, particularly for stochastic entities. Among categorical models, greedy decoding produces the highest rollout validity, while sampling from a next-token model yields the best-calibrated stochastic predictions. Failures in continuous models, such as disappearing game characters, echo those seen in more complex environments. Here, known dynamics let us measure their impact. In 3D, categorical models also achieve stronger long-horizon performance with less training compute. Even models with lossy tokenization remain competitive on semantic accuracy and FVD, despite lower next-frame RGB accuracy. Together, these findings make a strong case for categorical prediction as a compute-efficient route to learning world dynamics.

papers.title: Linear Response Theory of Nitrogen K-Edge X-ray Absorption of TCNQ
papers.summary: The linear response of the density is computed in the frequency domain within the generalized Kohn--Sham framework of adiabatic time-dependent density functional theory, employing hybrid exchange-correlation functionals. It is shown that the generalized Casida equations imply a Dyson-like equation for the linear-response of the full frequency-dependent one-electron reduced density matrix of the reference GKS system. We implement this formalism in the \textsc{Crystal} code and apply it to the nitrogen K-edge near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) of 7,7,8,8-tetracyano-$p$-quinodimethane (TCNQ), the acceptor in the charge-transfer salt TTF-TCNQ. We interpret the spectrum through a step-by-step construction by building blocks of increasing complexity. This procedure separates the effects of $π$ conjugation, of multiple equivalent absorbing centers and of the ring on the in-plane ($π_\parallel$) and out-of-plane ($π_\perp$) resonances. The theoretical result is confirmed by a comparison with angle-resolved experiments. In contrast with earlier assignments based only on the ground-state density of states, we find that the lowest-energy resonance is dominated by the ground-state KS LUMO contribution. Indeed, comparison with the independent-particle approximation shows that the exact-exchange contribution to the kernel is essential for a correct assignment of the peaks.

papers.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence with Learning Style Models: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has emerged as a powerful tool for transforming learning. This review examines how Generative AI can be integrated with established learning style models (VARK, Kolb, Felder-Silverman, and Honey & Mumford) to support student engagement in large online classes. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar (2015 to 2026) and included 41 studies that met the eligibility criteria. The review maps Generative AI capabilities to learning style preferences, synthesizes existing implementations, highlights benefits and challenges, and proposes pathways for future research and practice. Despite ongoing debates regarding the empirical validity of learning styles, Generative AI enables flexible, multimodal, and real-time adaptation. This study offers practical insights for educators and developers seeking to build more effective, learner centered learning systems

papers.title: Scalable Matrix-Free Algorithms for Variance Estimation of Survey-Weighted Survival Curves
papers.summary: Variance estimation for survey-weighted survival curves using existing statistical software can require substantial time and memory, particularly when the number of distinct event times is large. We developed two matrix-free algorithms that compute the conventional Taylor linearization variance estimator without constructing the full event-time covariance matrix: one accumulates individual-level linearization contributions, while the other directly updates aggregated contributions at the primary sampling unit (PSU) level. We evaluated numerical accuracy, runtime, and peak memory usage through an application to the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) and simulation experiments. Both approaches yielded survival and variance estimates identical to the R implementation. In the 7-year follow-up analysis of 7,608 NHATS participants with 2,879 deaths, computation time decreased from approximately 26 minutes to less than 3 seconds with the individual-level approach and less than 1 second with the PSU-level approach. Simulations with sample sizes of 1,000 to 10,000 showed similar results, with more pronounced computational advantages as sample size and the number of distinct event times increased. In more demanding settings, the existing implementation failed due to memory exhaustion, whereas both proposed approaches completed successfully. Matrix-free computation can improve the efficiency and scalability of design-based variance estimation while preserving numerical accuracy.

papers.title: Bayesian Bias Learning-Enabled Probabilistic Voltage Estimation with Unknown Uncertainty Modeling of DERs in Distribution Grids
papers.summary: One key challenge in distribution system state es- timation is unknown input statistics from the growing inte- gration of distributed energy resources (DERs), which may largely deviate from Gaussian uncertainty. Existing model-based estimators often rely on the assumption that all inputs follow known Gaussian distributions, while data-driven methods suffer from overfitting and failure in out-of-distribution scenarios. This paper proposes a Bayesian bias learning (BBL)-enabled probabilistic voltage estimation method in distribution systems with unknown DER generation statistics. The proposed learning- enabled method consists of two stages: probabilistic uncertainty inference and computationally efficient voltage estimation. First, a physics-constrained probabilistic density inference network is developed to learn Gaussian mixture representations of DER generation from historical data. Then, the resulting probabilistic representations, treated as pseudo-measurements, are integrated into a BBL-enabled voltage estimator via a decomposition- and-parallelization mechanism. Furthermore, utilizing a linear analytical solution, the proposed BBL-enabled voltage estimator efficiently captures linearization-induced biases and attains ac- curate probabilistic estimation. By integrating learning-enabled probabilistic uncertainty modeling into the parallel estimation structure, the proposed method achieves uncertainty-aware scal- able voltage estimation. Case studies on two unbalanced IEEE distribution networks show that the proposed estimator achieves significantly higher accuracy and computational efficiency under unknown uncertainty, outperforming recent data-driven and model-based methods.

papers.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Specification-guided reinforcement learning (RL) translates formal specifications of desired behavior of agents into shaped rewards. This paper introduces SLICR, a significant paradigm shift that advances the state of the art to specification-guided RL in adversarial settings under partial observability. We employ Strategy Logic (SL), which allows explicit quantification over agents' strategies and uses the linear temporal logic (LTL) to specify the agents' objectives and constraints. This enables reasoning not only about how agents should act to satisfy a specification, but also about how they should respond to the strategies and behaviors of other agents. We evaluate SLICR on three popular benchmarks: Predator-Prey, Google Research Football, and our home-grown extension of SMAC-HARD, demonstrating its effectiveness, scalability, and ability to adapt to diverse adversarial strategies.

papers.title: The $H^{2|2}$-model and the Anderson model with Cauchy potential: similarities and a conjectured relation
papers.summary: We highlight strange similarities between the Anderson model with Cauchy potential with energy-disorder parameters $(E,λ)$ and the $H^{2|2}$ supersymmetric sigma field with initial non local conductances proportional to $W_{x,y}=λ^2\left \vert \left (-Δ-E+ iλ)\right)_{x,y}^{-1}\right\vert^2$ where $Δ$ is the discrete Laplace operator. More precisely, looking at the Brownian interpolation of both, we show that they follow very similar equations. Motivated by that we investigate the different phases of the $H^{2|2}$-model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with conductances $rW$ for some $r>0$ and show that whatever $r>0$ the $H^{2|2}$-model displays localized and delocalized phases which are coherent with what is expected or proved for the Cauchy potential with energy-disorder parameters $(E,λ)$. Finally, we propose a conjecture that compares key quantities of the two models and would imply existence of delocalized regime for the Anderson model with Cauchy potential in dimension $d\ge 3$.

papers.title: OpenAHBU: Open-sourced Automatic Human Behaviour Understanding Toolkit Through Facial Behaviour Analysis
papers.summary: Automatic facial behaviour understanding (AFBU) is fundamental to various human-centred applications, yet existing academically available toolkits offer limited functionality, closed training pipelines, and weak generalisation. This paper presents OpenAHBU, a fully open-sourced, generalisable toolkit integrating 11 AFBU functions across three semantic levels: (i) short-term external facial attributes, including landmarks, blendshapes, Action Units, and expressions; (ii) short-term facial behaviour-related human psychological states, including valence/arousal and pain; and (iii) long-term facial behaviour-related psychological traits, including depression and personality. Particularly, we re-developed eight functions, where at least four deep learning models covering different computational complexities are developed for each function, providing flexible deployment on resource-constrained and high-throughput computing scenarios. More importantly, models of most functions are trained on a comprehensive corpus aggregating multiple academically available datasets, ensuring robust cross-dataset generalisability.In addition, we include a Synergistic Multi-task Enhancement (SMTE) module to efficiently and adaptively enhance each OpenAHBU function by leveraging the complementary cues contained in its most-related support function's predictions.Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our OpenAHBU outperformed existing open-source toolkits not only in functional coverage but also the predictive performances, while providing superior deployment flexibility across diverse computational scenarios.With fully publicly available training and inference scripts, pre-trained weights, user-friendly GUI, Python library, and cross-platform compatibility, our OpenAHBU provides a reproducible, scalable and extensible toolkit at https://github.com/OpenAHBU/OpenAHBU.

papers.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
papers.summary: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.

papers.title: Who Grades the Agent? Privilege Separation for Coding-Agent Benchmarks
papers.summary: Benchmarks for AI-based coding agents are a staple of the current AI landscape, because they are the leading way to measure the performance of LLMs. Their scores guide business and research decisions. Evaluating coding agents is challenging, since they are able to manipulate their evaluation infrastructure to artificially achieve better scores. Grading an agent's solution often requires running its code, which can then manipulate the evaluation process. BenchJack, an automated benchmark auditor, recently reached near-perfect scores on nine of ten popular agent benchmarks without actually solving their tasks. Agents already do this unprompted, as OpenAI's July 2026 Hugging Face incident showed. Building on secure systems design, we introduce SplitBench, a privilege separation framework for evaluating coding agents and the first in the scientific literature to separate running a task's tests from judging their results. Even an agent whose code takes over the entire test environment cannot forge a pass, because a trusted grader holds the expected answers. We show that real-world benchmarks (e.g., Terminal-Bench, DeepSWE) can be ported to the SplitBench framework with minimal effort and high fidelity: 180 of 202 tasks convert, and SplitBench agrees with the native graders on 98.7% of agent attempts. We attack the converted tasks in the worst case, where adversarial agents can read all the grading code but not the expected answers. SplitBench blocked 75% of their attempts; the rest mostly reveal weaknesses in the original tasks' tests rather than flaws in SplitBench.

papers.title: A sharp dimensional threshold for polygonal bubbling in an almost critical problem
papers.summary: In this paper we study sign-changing solutions for the problem $-Δu=|u|^{2^*-2-\varepsilon}u$ in $\mathcal B$, $u=0$ on $\partial\mathcal B$, where $\mathcal B$ is the unit ball of $\mathbb R^N$, $N\geq3$, $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter, so that the problem is slightly subcritical. In \cite{BDP}, Bartsch, D'Aprile and Pistoia proved that, in every dimension, there exist two solutions which blow up, as $\varepsilon\to0$, positively at the origin and negatively at two antipodal points; as a by-product of our approach, we prove their conjecture that the corresponding reduced energy has exactly two critical points, both nondegenerate, in every dimension. We consider the natural generalization in which the negative bubbles are located at the vertices of a regular $k$-gon, $k\geq3$, and we show that the picture changes drastically. When $k=3$ there is a sharp dimensional threshold: if $N\geq13$ the reduced energy has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate saddle point and a nondegenerate local minimum, which generate two distinct solutions, while if $3\leq N\leq12$ no solution of this type exists. When $k\geq4$ no solution of this type exists in any dimension. Moreover, for both families of solutions found for $k=3$ the nodal set stays uniformly away from $\partial\mathcal B$, in contrast with the case of two negative bubbles, where the nodal set of one of the two solutions touches the boundary, and with the Brezis--Nirenberg problem, where the nodal set of the solutions with the same configuration always reaches the boundary.

papers.title: ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts
papers.summary: Nautical charts encode safety-critical maritime information through standardized symbols, attributes, text, and heterogeneous geometries. Interpreting these charts and assessing the navigational significance of successive chart updates requires recognizing nautical features, determining their spatial relationships, and applying navigational knowledge. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising approach to nautical-chart interpretation, yet systematic evaluation of their fine-grained nautical feature recognition, chart-based spatial reasoning, and application of navigational knowledge to assessing chart changes remains limited. We introduce ENC-QA, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 77,312 questions derived from 6,612 National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Electronic Navigational Charts (ENCs). The benchmark evaluates four complementary capabilities: ENC Perception, Spatial Reasoning, Joint Perception and Spatial Reasoning, and Application. Of these, 8,227 questions form a progressive subset that decomposes selected chart-change cases into linked questions progressing from change detection to criticality assessment, enabling case-level analysis of how models use perceptual and spatial evidence to determine the navigational significance of chart changes. Evaluations of 10 open-weight VLMs reveal substantial limitations in fine-grained nautical feature recognition and feature-grounded spatial reasoning. Controlled evidence interventions show that relevant perceptual and spatial information improves change-criticality accuracy. Our findings establish ENC-QA as a diagnostic resource for nautical-chart understanding and safety-critical navigational decisions. We will release the benchmark and evaluation code upon publication.

papers.title: Feasibility study of two-stage direct laser acceleration of electrons
papers.summary: We present the first numerical demonstration of two-stage direct laser acceleration (DLA) of electrons. The result was obtained using quasi-3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. The first stage ($a_0 = 6$, $τ= 200~\mathrm{fs}$, $w = 4λ$, $λ= 0.8~μ\mathrm{m}$) utilized a nitrogen gas target with an atomic density of $n_a = 0.008n_{cr}$. This stage was designed to accelerate low-energy electrons, achieving a maximum energy of approximately 94 MeV with a two-temperature energy spectrum ($T_1 = 7.0$ MeV and $T_2 = 16.0$ MeV) and a charge of 6.04 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The resulting electron bunch was then injected into the second stage, where hydrogen at a lower density ($n_a = 0.01n_{cr}$) was used, while the laser parameters were the same as in the first stage except that the waist was increased to $w = 8λ$. After the second stage, the electrons reached energies up to 225 MeV, with a two-temperature energy spectrum ($T_1 = 18.4$ MeV and $T_2 = 88.3$ MeV) and a charge of 4.55 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The self-injected electrons in the second stage reached a maximum energy of 123 MeV with a charge of 1.14 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The simulation results are compared with a theoretical DLA model, which describes the electron motion in the combined fields of the laser pulse and the quasistatic plasma channel. The model accounts for the transverse size of the channel by incorporating a Gaussian attenuation of the channel fields and off-axis injection. The theoretical model correctly describes the observed acceleration dynamics for both low-energy and pre-accelerated electrons, confirming its validity for designing multi-stage DLA schemes. Thus, the implementation of multi-stage acceleration by the DLA mechanism is successfully demonstrated for the first time in a numerical experiment.

papers.title: Hotter than Little Red Dots: Two Quasars with $T\sim10^4\,\mathrm{K}$ blackbody-like continua at $z\sim4$
papers.summary: Gas envelope models of Little Red Dots (LRDs) predict a transition from cool ($T\sim5000\,\mathrm{K}$), gas-enshrouded accretion to an exposed quasar, but observational candidates remain scarce. We identify two blackbody quasars (BBQs), JADES1180 at $z=3.711$ and GTO1215 at $z=4.552$, among 3,553 sources with archival NIRSpec/PRISM spectra. Both show extremely red rest-frame UV ($β_\mathrm{UV}>2.0$) but blue optical continua ($β_\mathrm{opt}<-0.75$), where $f_λ\proptoλ^β$. Their $Λ$-shaped UV-optical continua peak at $λ\approx3000-4000$ Å and are not reproduced by a quasar template reddened with an SMC-like extinction curve.
