Our method achieves success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on the three benchmarks, respectively. Real-world evaluation further yields an average success rate of 96.7% across three manipulation tasks. These results highlight the potential of Embodied-Harness to improve robotic manipulation through experience-driven harness self-improvement.

papers.title: Exchange rights and vacancy priorities
papers.summary: Many institutions let incumbents exchange positions while allocating announced vacancies by priority, withdrawing positions released by vacancy recipients. A policy specifies permitted exchanges, vacancy eligibility, and priorities. A strategy-proof, individually rational rule protecting exchange rights and vacancy priorities exists precisely for policies without conflict cycles. Restricting protection to first choices does not enlarge this class. We introduce the propose-and-trade rule, which satisfies these properties and selects the applicant-optimal core allocation under every conflict-free policy. We identify when propose-and-trade is the unique strategy-proof, individually rational rule protecting first choices. These axioms characterize deferred acceptance and top trading cycles in their classic settings. Under a policy with a conflict cycle, propose-and-trade is manipulable but protects exchange rights and first-choice claims. Replacing it with any strategy-proof rule makes some applicant worse off at some profile. We show when priority reform alone can eliminate conflict cycles and when eligibility or exchange permissions must change.

papers.title: Zeroing in on BSM at Colliders
papers.summary: Destructive interference between light and heavy dynamics can produce a zero in the amplitude which, for strongly coupled UV completions, lies parametrically below the heavy threshold. We identify under which assumptions this parametrically light zero exists, and when it admits an effective field theory description. We study how absorptive effects and helicity structure affect the existence of the zero and turn it into a dip. When the dip is kinematically accessible, we show how its position, depth, and curvature constrain the UV dynamics. Collider examples illustrate the importance of interference in indirect searches and the information available when the zero is kinematically accessible.

papers.title: Characterisation of B-type stars in four young Galactic open clusters. II. Photometric variability with TESS and identification of pulsating stars
papers.summary: Pulsations and binarity are important properties of massive stars and influence their structure and evolution. Young open clusters are ideal laboratories to study massive stars, since they are mostly coeval and chemically homogeneous. We analyse 82 B-type stars in the Galactic open clusters $h$ and $χ$ Persei, NGC 457, NGC 581, and NGC 1960, which have ages between 15 and 30 Myr. We extract light curves using both simple aperture photometry and a point-spread-function-based method that minimises contamination from crowded fields in full-frame images from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. We successfully extract light curves for 63 stars. The majority have photometric variability caused by pulsations, showing how pulsations are a common property of young B-type stars in clusters. We classify stars into different pulsator types based on their spectral type and frequency spectrum. The most common pulsator class are beta Cephei stars, with 29 stars in total, and we discover pulsation modes in almost all stars with a spectral type of B2 or earlier. All Be stars show pulsations, which supports the consensus of the ubiquity of pulsations in these stars. Finally, we confirm that the majority of early B-type stars are in binary systems, except for two pulsating Be stars and a star with rotational modulation. This indicates that pulsations do not significantly bias the spectroscopic detection of short-period binaries, except for Be stars where the spectroscopic radial velocity variability threshold should be higher than the typical value of 20 km s$^{-1}$.

papers.title: Too Fast to Doubt? Skipping Reasoning Leaves Jev-like Models Vulnerable
papers.summary: Fast decision models offer low-latency actions and explicit confidence estimates. We audit four state-of-the-art decision models on 1,440 paired synthetic browser tasks, injecting false conclusions or evidence interpretations through external comments. Across models, clean accuracy averages 91.0%, yet two-shot attack success reaches 81.2%. Mean expected calibration error rises from 2.6% on clean inputs to 36.7% under conclusion poisoning and 36.1% under evidence poisoning. Clean accuracy and calibration therefore do not ensure reliable decisions under injection. We further compare GPT-6 Luna and Luna Decisions, which share the same base model, on 48 matched tasks. With a chain of thought averaging fewer than 30 reasoning tokens per response, low-effort GPT-6 Luna answers 95.83% of poisoned inputs correctly, versus 38.54% for native Luna Decisions, while mean selected-generation latency increases from 0.29 to 1.94 seconds. These results expose a sharp latency-robustness trade-off: skipping reasoning for sub-second speed leaves fast decision models substantially more vulnerable to deceptive web content.

papers.title: PHOTO-CAT - Photometric Contamination Analyzer Tool: A High-Performance Framework for Photometric Contamination Assessment
papers.summary: High-precision photometric missions are sensitive to flux contamination from neighboring stars, which can bias light curves, dilute transit depths, and compromise photometric precision. We present PHOTO-CAT, a catalog-driven, mission-agnostic tool for quantifying stellar flux contamination in photometric observations. The tool builds a three-dimensional Euclidean representation of the sky from a user-provided astrometric catalog, indexes it with a memory-optimized KDTree for rapid neighbor searches, and computes per-target contamination metrics from angular separation, relative fluxes, and configurable aperture models (top-hat or circular Gaussian PSF), optionally converted into an arbitrary instrumental bandpass via empirical photometric relations or stellar spectral models. A streaming, CSR-style storage format with compact internal identifiers enables scalable processing of catalogs with tens to hundreds of millions of sources with minimal memory overhead. Outputs include per-target contaminating flux, contamination ratios, target purity, number of neighboring sources, and their angular separations, supporting target screening and field-selection decisions ahead of observations. We demonstrate the software performance on all-sky Gaia samples (G <= 12, with neighbors down to G = 17; over three million targets), providing global contamination statistics and spatial characterization of crowded regions, and apply it to the Ariel Mission Candidate Sample to show how wavelength-dependent contamination estimates support target selection and observing-geometry optimization. Although developed for the Mauve satellite, PHOTO-CAT is mission-agnostic and readily applicable to TESS, PLATO, Ariel, and other surveys.
papers.comment: Article accepted for pubblication by RASTI with official acceptance date 20/11/2026

papers.title: CanopyFormer: Attention-Guided SegFormer for Explainable Forest Cover Segmentation
papers.summary: In transformer segmentation models, attention is usually visualized after training rather than supervised. Although attention supervision has been explored for natural images and driving scenes, aerial forest segmentation typically uses attention only as an architectural component and evaluates interpretability qualitatively. We present CanopyFormer, an attention-guided SegFormer-B0 that uses an Attention Consistency Loss to align attention with the ground-truth forest mask, encouraging attention to focus on canopy regions. Since SegFormer uses spatial-reduction attention, we adapt Gradient-weighted Attention Rollout by restricting it to the final encoder stage, where the attention matrix is square. We introduce Average Attention-Mask Overlap (AAMO) to measure attention alignment and incorporate a deletion test to evaluate faithfulness. On 5108 images, our method increases AAMO from 0.0334 to 0.7476, approximately 22 times the vanilla SegFormer-B0 result, with a modest decrease in Dice score from 0.8743 to 0.8577. The deletion test reveals that improved alignment does not necessarily translate into improved faithfulness: removing the most-attended 25% of patches reduces the forest score by 12.1%, compared with 33.0% when removing random patches. Attention supervision introduces no additional inference cost, although double backpropagation makes each training step 2.6 to 2.8 times slower. The attention alignment improvement also generalizes to a second dataset, LoveDA. Additionally, a Boundary Refinement Module provides no consistent Dice improvement and reduces AAMO, while mean squared error substantially outperforms Kullback-Leibler divergence as the attention loss.

papers.title: Hy-MT3: More Accurate, Robust and Practical Multilingual Translation Models in the Wild
papers.summary: Hy-MT3 is the third generation of the Hunyuan multilingual translation model family, including \textbf{Hy-MT3-1.8B}, \textbf{Hy-MT3-7B} and \textbf{Hy-MT3-30B-A3B (MoE)}. Compared with Hy-MT2, Hy-MT3 translates \textbf{more accurately, more completely and more faithfully to user constraints}: on real-world scenario data, the share of samples with mistranslations is reduced by \textbf{43\%}, omissions or additions by \textbf{74\%}, and instruction-following errors by \textbf{40\%}, while language coverage is expanded from \textbf{38 to 102} languages. With only 3B activated parameters, \textbf{Hy-MT3-30B-A3B achieves the best overall performance among all evaluated models in non-thinking mode}, including flagship models such as Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi-K3.1-Pro and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and approaches the strongest closed-source thinking models such as GPT-6.1-Sol and Gemini-4-Argon, while surpassing models that consume \textbf{more than 30$\times$} its inference compute. Beyond general translation, Hy-MT3 is optimized for two industrial scenarios. For \textbf{game localization}, built with high-quality game-domain data and a professional evaluation system from the Honor of Kings team, Hy-MT3-30B-A3B matches or outperforms strong closed-source models such as Gemini 3.1 Pro on all core metrics, and can be plugged into game development pipelines through an open-source toolchain. For \textbf{image translation}, Hy-MT3 improves context understanding and error correction to better tolerate OCR errors, achieving the best result among models of comparable size. Finally, we open-source \textbf{TransRubric}, a rubric-based automatic evaluation suite for translation, which outperforms other evaluation schemes on the WMT26 metrics shared task test set and is more stable with respect to human evaluation.

papers.title: Closed-loop policy optimisation for cylinder wake control via differentiable simulation
papers.summary: Suppressing vortex shedding behind a circular cylinder is a classical problem in active flow control.Model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL) learns such policies by interacting with the flow without differentiating its dynamics, which typically requires a large interaction budget. This study optimises closed-loop policies by differentiable simulation: control-loss gradients propagate through the simulated flow to the policy parameters, which are updated by reverse-mode automatic differentiation. The policy maps local velocity measurements to a jet amplitude imposed through differentiable synthetic-jet boundary conditions. In a two-dimensional confined cylinder wake at Rey=100, eight policy updates (about 78 shedding periods of forward simulation) give approximately 8% drag reduction and 99.6% suppression of lift fluctuations, the drag level being comparable to reported DRL results. Suppression is sustained by feedback: a mean-matched constant jet does not maintain it, whereas the same policy responds similarly at three activation phases and recovers after upstream disturbances. A velocity-deviation reward alone retains strong suppression, and observations of two instantaneous velocity components at one near-wake or surface location reach about 99.8% suppression, whereas a single surface pressure leaves residual oscillations. Together with related DRL results, this suggests that reward and observation requirements here are set by policy optimisation and flow physics.

papers.title: Nuclear Precision and Multimessenger Constraints on Neutron-Star Structure
papers.summary: Neutron-star cores retain structural freedom beyond the constraints supplied by nuclear measurements. We quantify this freedom through an observable-dependent variance ceiling and identify radius--Love compensation as a mechanism suppressing nuclear constraints on tides. Across four data-conditioned equation-of-state families, a pulsar radius measured to 0.3 km paired with a binary tide measured to 10\% removes 44--68\% of the current logarithmic Love-number variance. The framework connects laboratory precision and complementary stellar measurements to core structure.

papers.title: Statistical and Machine Learning Approaches for Estimating Visitation to Natural Spaces in the UK
papers.summary: Natural spaces support health and well-being, but increasing recreational use can put pressure on ecologically sensitive sites. Understanding when, where and why people visit is important for planning, site management and evaluating interventions. Building on work by the Office for National Statistics, we developed statistical and machine learning models to predict visitor numbers at points located in natural spaces. We trained on automated people counter data across a range of green and blue spaces in England and Wales and tested the models' ability to generalise to unseen counter locations. Our models offer a scalable approach for predicting visitor numbers in natural spaces, reducing reliance on surveys and physical counters.

papers.title: On Robust Strictly Positive Real Synthesis for High-Order Interval Polynomials
papers.summary: We establish two complementary results on common strictly positive real (SPR) numerators for Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial families. First, for every order $n \ge 10$, we construct a monic Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial family with rational endpoints and positive width in every nonleading coefficient such that every nonzero real numerator of degree at most $n$ produces a strictly negative real part at some member and some positive frequency. In particular, robust Hurwitz stability alone does not guarantee equal-degree SPR synthesis in high orders. Second, for every order $n \ge 1$, we prove that a common real SPR numerator of exact degree $n$ always exists whenever the lower endpoint of each interior coefficient interval is at most $10^{-5}$ times its upper endpoint, while the constant and leading coefficients vary over arbitrary compact positive intervals.

papers.title: Deep conditional distribution estimation via nonparametric exponential tilt models
papers.summary: Estimating the conditional distribution of a response $Y$ given covariates $X$ is a fundamental problem in statistics, underlying prediction, feature estimation, and dependence assessment. We propose a unified nonparametric representation of the conditional density, a nonparametric exponential tilt model, in which the dependence between $Y$ and $X$ is captured by an interaction function $φ(x,y)$ while both baseline densities are left unspecified. We establish identifiability and develop a nonparametric likelihood method that profiles out the baselines by empirical likelihood, with non-asymptotic error bounds under general sieve conditions. Because the profile likelihood admits no closed-form or readily tractable population counterpart, standard empirical process arguments do not apply; we therefore establish a new exponential tail bound for the supremum of a canonical U-process under a uniform entropy condition, a result we show to be new to the U-process literature and of independent interest, with a largely self-contained proof. The framework unifies several inferential tasks: mutual density ratio and mutual information estimation; a general theory for conditional features, including means, quantiles and distribution functions, without separate smoothness assumptions on the individual conditional feature functions; and a finite-sample valid permutation test of independence. Under deep neural network sieves, the convergence rates depend on the intrinsic complexity of $φ$ rather than the ambient dimension. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method attains uniformly smaller estimation errors than existing conditional density and mutual density-ratio estimators, and delivers markedly higher power in independence testing when dependence is oscillatory or high-dimensional, while remaining comparable to established tests in standard settings.

papers.title: Detection of genuine multipartite entanglement by means of entanglement monotones
papers.summary: We look for pure state entanglement monotones that may serve as certificates of a strong form of genuine multipartite entanglement, that we refer to as irreducible entanglement: a $D$-partite state (with $D\geq 3$) is irreducibly $D$-partite entangled if it cannot be decomposed as a product of states that are at most $(D-1)$-partite entangled. We start by establishing a no-go result proving that no reasonable genuine multipartite entanglement entropy can simultaneously obey LOCC-monotonicity and subadditivity. After relaxing the first condition to LO-monotonicity, we provide a simple method generating genuine multipartite entanglement monotones with the desired properties. Focusing on a subfamily of these monotones, we show that they are able to detect any form of genuine tripartite entanglement in three-qubit systems.

papers.title: Hierarchical Agentic Mid-Band Agility for Reliable Low-Latency Space-Air-Ground Integrated V2X Networks
papers.summary: Upper-mid-band spectrum offers bandwidth opportunities for the integrated networks of ground vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to support 6G wide-area vehicle-to-everything (V2X) connectivity. However, V2X services' latency and reliability are sensitive to the mid-band selection due to frequency-dependent propagation and rain attenuation. This paper investigates environment-aware spectrum agility over candidate frequency range 3 (FR3) bands within 7.125-24.25 GHz, jointly with end-to-end (E2E) multi-path traffic splitting and transmit power control. Each data packet is partitioned into non-overlapping subflows over direct and UAV-assisted paths, with failed sky-link subflows selectively retransmitted subject to retransmission and freshness constraints. We formulate latency- and reliability-oriented problems, followed by a unified sequential optimization problem incorporating band-switching costs and average quality-of-service (QoS) violation budgets. To coordinate optimization decisions across heterogeneous timescales, we develop an agentic AI-assisted hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (AA-HMARL) framework. A high-level agentic supervisor integrates recurrent memory, analytical evaluation of candidate bands, and event-triggered replanning to coordinate slow environmental adaptation with fast channel and retransmission dynamics, while distributed ground vehicles and UAV agents optimize data splitting and power using constrained MAPPO. Simulation results demonstrate an adjustable reliability-latency trade-off. Particularly, AA-HMARL reduces the mean E2E completion latency and the mean number of retransmission rounds among successfully delivered updates by 17.8-25.5% and 57.6-61.5%, respectively, and reduces the mean age of information (AoI) by 12.7-14.6% relative to fixed-band MAPPO across two traffic types.
papers.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. 13 pages, 9 figures

papers.title: Capillary partitioning of solutes on conformally coated colloidal monolayers: a universal geometric threshold
papers.summary: Depositing a conformal solid film on a hexagonal monolayer of spheres progressively closes the interstitial pores, and this closure controls where a dilute solute spin-coated from a volatile solvent ends up after drying: buried in the interstitial valleys or spread over the exposed caps. We derive the fraction of solute that ends in the valleys from first principles, for any sphere radius, film thickness and wetting liquid. The control parameter is the film thickness divided by the sphere radius, and a purely geometric threshold, about 0.155, separates two regimes for all sphere sizes. Below it, the three-sphere interstice is an open cup that the liquid fills through a narrow throat at the sphere equator, and about nine tenths of the solute end in the valleys. Above it, the throat pinches shut, sealing the cup and leaving only a shallow surface dimple, so this fraction drops more than twofold, never to recover. Treating the throat as a nearly triangular duct gives a closed-form filling rate, confirmed by exact flow calculations. During spin-coating, filling outpaces drying by up to five orders of magnitude, except within a fraction of a nanometre of the threshold. Partitioning is therefore set by capacity alone, through a one-parameter ratio of exact void volumes, identical for all sphere sizes. Thin-film simulations confirm the direction of liquid transport. For dye in ethanol on tantalum-pentoxide-coated polystyrene lattices, the predicted on-cap fraction rises from 0.06 to 0.76 across the threshold, agreeing at both ends with values inferred from measured Purcell factors.

papers.title: Combining Past Experimental Data for Efficient Estimation: A Shrinkage Approach
papers.summary: Firms routinely conduct randomized experiments, creating archives that could improve treatment-effect estimation in new experiments. However, past experiments evaluate related but different interventions, so their estimates may be biased for the current target. We study when and how borrowing from multiple auxiliary experiments can reduce the mean squared error (MSE) of a single treatment-effect estimate. In the oracle case, when biases and variances are known, borrowing from even one biased experiment strictly reduces MSE. In practice, we propose three shrinkage estimators and characterize their asymptotic MSE as the number of auxiliary experiments grows. Our analysis shows that average auxiliary bias and cross-study bias dispersion affect the relative performance of these estimators. As expected, smaller average bias magnitude generally improves performance. Surprisingly, bias dispersion can both benefit and harm our first estimator, the general plug-in estimator. On one hand, a more dispersed bias allows flexibility in cancelling the bias. On the other hand, the bias cancellation is imperfect as we only have an estimate of the bias, leading to overfitting. Motivated by this tradeoff, we propose a pooled plug-in estimator that restricts study-specific reweighting to limit this overfitting. However, both plug-in estimators can perform poorly when average bias is large. To address this, we develop a fixed-weight estimator with a hypothesis-testing gate that borrows only when the aggregate auxiliary mean is not significantly different from the target mean. Simulations illustrate the relative strengths of these estimators across bias environments and the relevance of the limiting analysis for finite collections of experiments. We also provide managerial guidance on which shrinkage estimator to use based on average bias and bias dispersion.

papers.title: Modeling the contact area and intersurface forces between Pb nanoparticles and suspended graphene
papers.summary: We perform large-scale atomistic simulations to explore the contact mechanics of Pb nanoparticles (NPs) physisorbed on a suspended graphene sheet at zero external load. The study considers the kinetics of the NPs' relative contact area and the distributions of intersurface atomic force magnitudes acting on the NP during self-assembly from the liquid phase, and the size scaling of these quantities for the solidified NPs. The functional forms of both the repulsive and attractive parts of the normal intersurface force distributions for solidified NPs are size-independent for nanoislands with a linear lateral size larger than about 10 nm (or a surface area-to-volume ratio less than about 1 nm$^{-1}$). To first order, the repulsive tail decays exponentially, while the cutoff power law fits more precisely, especially for the high-probability repulsive forces. In both cases, the decay exponent is around -5 nN$^{-1}$. The exponentially modified Gaussian is the best fit for the attractive part for most NP sizes. The time-averaged relative contact area calculated directly in the simulations shows considerable fluctuations for NPs a few nm in diameter, while converging to approximately 0.44 for larger NPs. Based on fitting the normal-force distributions, we obtain analytical expressions for the relative contact area. Ensemble-averaged relative contact areas for NPs larger than around 10 nm, calculated using the analytical expressions, match the time-averaged MD values within statistical error. Our model is the first step towards developing analytical approximations for quantitative estimates of the relative contact area of Pb NPs adsorbed on suspended graphene.

papers.title: Auditing Post-Training Unlearning in Diffusion Language Models using Sparse Autoencoders
papers.summary: Machine unlearning is an approach to privacy protection: it aims to remove the influence of designated data while preserving the model's behavior on information that should be retained. While a growing body of work investigates this objective in autoregressive large language models, machine unlearning remains underexplored in diffusion language models (DLMs). DLMs generate text through iterative denoising, exposing partially masked states whose internal representations change throughout the generation process. This raises a DLM-specific question: can selective forgetting improve by identifying forget-data-associated features and adapting their suppression across denoising stages? We conduct a controlled investigation of this question in LLaDA-8B-Instruct. To evaluate the unlearning of knowledge plausibly encoded during pre-training, we use WMDP as our forget-domain benchmark. Using top-k sparse autoencoders and denoising-state replay, we compare static and stage-adaptive feature suppression. We find substantial shifts in forget-data-associated features across denoising stages, but tracking these dynamics alone does not reliably improve the forget-retain trade-off at the evaluated operating points. Together, our study provides an initial empirical foundation for developing and evaluating machine unlearning as a post-training privacy mechanism in DLMs.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 1 figure. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Inference-Time AI Privacy (InfPriv 2026)

papers.title: Coronagraphic time-delay interferometry: fundamental steps towards concrete applications
papers.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a future space-based gravitational wave (GW) observatory. Central to LISA data analysis is time-delay interferometry (TDI), which reduces otherwise overwhelming laser frequency noise. In previous work, we explored coronagraphic TDI, a sky-dependent null-stream channel which cancels the GW signal of a point-like source when pointed at its sky position. Because this property relies only on the geometric response of LISA, coronagraphic TDI is a candidate for model-agnostic sky localization. Here, we address three challenges which arise when analyzing realistic LISA data: (i) spacecraft motion; (ii) signal superposition; (iii) instrumental noise. We derive a second-generation coronagraphic TDI variable and its analytic noise model, and show that it reduces laser frequency noise in the presence of spacecraft motion while still recovering the position of the source. Using pairs of Galactic binaries (GBs), we find that sources can be localized independently provided they do not overlap in frequency, even when they share the same sky position, whereas sources overlapping in frequency can only be localized if one dominates by a factor of ~100 in amplitude. This is confirmed by the analysis of a simulation containing a massive black hole binary and 49 verification GBs. Finally, we introduce a statistical test based on the analytic noise model, which provides well-calibrated confidence regions for the sky position of the source. Applying it to GBs in the presence of instrumental noise, we find that the geometric response alone only weakly constrains the sky position: even at signal-to-noise ratios of order 10^4, 90% confidence regions span ~10^3 deg^2. These are fundamental steps towards applications of coronagraphic TDI to LISA data, such as sky localization and glitch discrimination, which we discuss.

papers.title: Emergent Causality of Macroscopic Transport and Equilibration in Long-Range Quantum Systems
papers.summary: Long-range couplings in quantum many-body systems challenge conventional notions of locality and causality. Here, we show that macroscopic particle transport nevertheless exhibits emergent causality --- an effective light cone that becomes strict in the thermodynamic limit. For power-law hopping with a decay exponent $α\in(D,D+1)$ in $D$ spatial dimensions, the emergent causality cone expands super-ballistically, and we establish that its scaling is optimal. Our results imply lower bounds on the equilibration time of long-range systems. Finally, we construct an example of a long-range free-fermion chain with $α\in (1,3/2)$, whose macroscopic density equilibrates super-ballistically, i.e., in a time sub-linear in the system size. While long-range interactions are usually associated with slow equilibration due to increased energy barriers, our example demonstrates that long-range hopping can lead to accelerated equilibration.

papers.title: Trust What Repeats: Capped World-Model Policy Gradients for Humanoid Motion Tracking
papers.summary: Training a humanoid motion tracker by backpropagating imagined returns through a learned world model is fast, because the model gives a first-order policy gradient. We ask how much of that gradient holds in the simulator. On a tracker for the Unitree G1, the $0.5\%$ of imagined rollouts with the largest gradients carry $22\%$ of the summed gradient norm, yet neither a second rollout from the same state nor the simulator confirms them. When the actions are moved along the model's gradient, the simulator returns 94% of the predicted change in return where the gradient norm is below the batch median, 48% between 3 and 10 times the median, and 1% above 30 times; the part of a gradient that either check confirms stops growing at a few times the median. We therefore cap each rollout's action-gradient norm at 10 times the batch median, draw imagination starts in proportion to their predicted gradient norm so that the cap removes less, and reset episodes where the world model and critic predict the lowest return. Trained on 223 hours of motion and tested on 353 motions that no actor performed in training, the method raises the normalized return of SuperMimic, the baseline it builds on, from 0.953 to 0.967 and the lowest $1\%$ of test clips from 0.65 to 0.76, halves the test clips that fall persistently, from 15--18 to 7--10, and reaches the baseline's final return in 40% of the baseline's iterations and half its training time. On LAFAN1, trained and evaluated on the same clips as prior work, it reaches 0.935 against 0.906.

papers.title: Cyclic perturbations encode memories in trained neural networks without loss of performance
papers.summary: Many disordered materials exhibit a remarkable form of memory: they retain information about the history of cyclic perturbations. Whether this phenomenon also occurs in artificial neural networks, whose mathematical structure and dynamics share many similarities with disordered physical systems, is unknown. Here we show that cyclically perturbing a trained, overparameterized deep neural network encodes information in the structure of the weights that can subsequently be retrieved, thus retaining memory of the perturbation history. During each write cycle, all weights are displaced, after which the network relaxes through gradient descent. Repeated cycles organise the neural network into a state that is reversible for perturbations up to the write amplitude, allowing the encoded value to be read from the onset of irreversible weight motion. Multiple memories can also be encoded, although under deterministic writing only the largest persists at long times. Inspired by cyclically sheared suspensions, we introduce a novel noisy-write protocol that preserves all encoded memories at long times. Remarkably, neither deterministic nor noisy memory writing measurably affects the network's performance on unseen data from its original learning task. Our results establish cyclic memory as a phenomenon shared by disordered physical systems and deep neural networks, and show that networks can exploit as yet unexplored memory capabilities without compromising their original function.

papers.title: A nonlinear transient finite element analysis of coupled solvent diffusion and large deformation of magneto-elastic hydrogel balloon
papers.summary: This study investigates the transient swelling of an initially spherical magnetoelastic hydrogel balloon. The balloon is inflated at constant internal pressure and exposed to the non-uniform magnetic field of one or two current-carrying coils. The gel is modelled as a compressible Ogden network mixed with solvent through Flory--Huggins theory, with an additive elastic--mixing--magnetic decomposition of the free energy. A fully coupled nonlinear finite element formulation uses a staggered solution scheme and a Taylor--Hood-type discretisation. It follows the balloon from its dry inflated state to either swollen equilibrium or burst. The formulation recovers the analytical free-swelling stretch and the delayed-burst regime, and its converged states agree with equilibrium energy minimisation. Symmetry-breaking (pear-shaped) dry configurations do not survive swelling: they rearrange rapidly and then relax by diffusion onto the symmetric branch. Transient membrane stresses can exceed their equilibrium values by nearly an order of magnitude. For coils which are sufficiently close to undeformed balloon, fields beyond a critical intensity close the slow-inflation curve into a loop. Stable swollen equilibria then exist only within a bounded pressure window that narrows as the field increases, and outside of it the balloon bursts. Under two coaxial coils, asymmetry about the equator appears only when the coils differ in current or radius. The magnetic field therefore acts as a control parameter for shape of balloon and permits or prevents stable swelling at a given pressure.

papers.title: Hints of planet formation in progress around DR Tau from observations with LBT SHARK-NIR and SHARK-VIS
papers.summary: Protoplanetary disks are the primary sites of planet formation. However, the direct imaging of protoplanets still embedded within their parental disks remains a significant challenge, with only a small number of confirmed detections to date and several candidates awaiting verification. We search for embedded planets in the protoplanetary disk of the young star DRTau by targeting accretion signatures from forming sub-stellar objects. Using narrow-band imaging, we observe both visible Halpha and near-infrared Paschen-beta (Pabeta) emission to identify actively accreting companions. To this end, we performed high-contrast observations of DRTau using the SHARK-VIS (0.40-0.95 micron) and SHARK-NIR (0.96-1.70 micron) imagers at the LBT. The study uses a combination of narrow-band filters to isolate accretion signatures and broad-band filters for multi-wavelength characterization in both the visible and near-infrared. Our observations recover the primary disk structures previously identified in the literature, albeit at low signal-to-noise (S/N). We identify two compact features with S/N between 6 and 13 in both narrow- and broad-band filters. The first, an elongated structure, matches previous SPHERE detections, while the second, more compact feature, is now confirmed despite its low S/N in earlier datasets. A comparison over a seven-year baseline confirms the stability of both structures. Their observed orbital motion is consistent with Keplerian rotation, potentially suggesting the presence of an undetected planetary-mass companion (few MJup) at the location of the second feature. However, our analysis does not confirm Halpha or Pabeta emission originating from localized accretion. Instead, we conclude that the observed flux is likely stellar light reflected by dust at these locations and discuss alternative mechanisms that could account for such detections.
papers.comment: 12 pages; 10 Figures; Accepted for publications on A&A

papers.title: Ancilla-Free Exact Dicke-State Synthesis with Optimal Size and Depth
papers.summary: We construct exact circuits for $n$-qubit Dicke states of any Hamming weight $k$ using $O(n)$ single-qubit gates and CNOTs in $O(\log n)$ depth without ancillary qubits. The gate count and depth are asymptotically optimal for every $0<k<n$. We compress symmetric blocks to free output qubits for weight-dependent phases. A sign correction followed by a collective rotation produces a state whose overlap with the target is at least a positive constant, so exact amplitude amplification takes $O(1)$ steps. For balanced Dicke states ($k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$), the logarithmic depth disproves the $Ω(k)$ depth lower bound conjectured by Yuan and Zhang (2025).

papers.title: SOAR: Training-Free Rank-Consistent Rollout Compression for Latent World Model Planning
papers.summary: Latent world models plan by rolling out hundreds of candidate action sequences through a transformer predictor, so a single decision can take tens of seconds. Existing accelerations prune spatial tokens as in vision-language models, yet a sampling-based planner uses predicted costs only to rank candidates, so a rollout can be compressed freely as long as the ranking survives. We propose SOAR, a training-free method that adapts rollout compression to each planning decision. At every decision, SOAR probes a few candidates under several token budgets and keeps the smallest budget that preserves their ranking, so it compresses as far as the current decision allows, without task labels. A closed-loop study of more than 80,000 episodes fixes the rest of the rollout: the first step, which alone reads a real observation, stays exact, and the context frame is cached rather than recomputed. On seven navigation and manipulation tasks with frozen checkpoints, SOAR matches dense-level planning success at 2.3x speedup and retains 98% at 2.5x. Our code is available at https://github.com/starrywiki/SOAR.
papers.comment: 16 pages, including supplementary material. Anqi Li and Kai Liu contributed equally

papers.title: Seeing Is Not Steering: Where Verifiable Reasoning Can Enter an End-to-End Driving Planner
papers.summary: Driving models that reason may describe a hazard correctly while choosing their path for other reasons. We study where scene reasoning can enter an end-to-end planner so its influence can be checked. We freeze Drive-JEPA and use a fine-tuned vision-language model to state scene facts. Although fine-tuning improves fact accuracy, the two learned components we test show no detectable benefit from reading them. A rule-based fact check instead rejects or shortens paths that contradict the facts, linking each intervention to a stated fact. On the frozen planner alone, it gains 2.4 EPDMS points on navhard. Its 2.0-point margin over a control that changes the same frames without consulting facts remains statistically uncertain. A diagnostic using exact facts from maps and annotations yields a 3.6-point margin over its corresponding control, with a 95% confidence interval above zero. Separately, a path scorer and plan memory that read no stated facts raise navhard from 41.2 to 51.8. Bounding travel distance using the reasoner's facts adds 0.3 there and reduces navtest by 2.0. The fact check makes each intervention auditable, while the driving value of the reasoner's facts remains unresolved.

papers.title: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization benchmark problems from mixed Hamming packings
papers.summary: Benchmarking exact solvers and noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) requires small yet challenging instances, preferably coming from actual applications. We propose such a benchmark set derived from mixed Hamming packing, a hard problem in coding theory. Starting from its mixed-integer linear programming formulation, we provide a generator for the equivalent QUBO models and study 133 instances whose optima are certified by that formulation. In the feature space of the MQLib library, we position a broad range of existing quantum-oriented benchmarks relative to the classical ones: they lie along a narrow, sparse border of the region covered by MQLib, whereas our instances form a coherent family in a region that both collections leave almost empty. Classical heuristics and a simulated bifurcation machine find the optimum of most instances quickly, in several cases sooner than an exact mixed-integer solver first encounters it, suggesting heuristic warm starts for exact solvers; for an exact QUBO solver, in turn, it appears challenging to prove optimality. In Ising form, the instances are densely connected antiferromagnets whose large local fields are almost exactly balanced by the couplings, so that the decision on each variable rests on a small remainder. This makes them hard to embed and to represent accurately on current quantum annealers, in line with our D-Wave experiments.
papers.comment: 36 pages, 4 figures, 'Online resource 1' included at the end of the paper

papers.title: Chromatic calorimetry using nanocomposites: status and future challenges
papers.summary: The development of advanced detector technologies will play a key role in future high-energy physics experiments, such as the FCC-ee. In this context, chromatic calorimetry is an emerging concept for electromagnetic calorimeters, with the potential to combine the precise energy measurement of homogeneous calorimeters with longitudinal reconstruction of particle showers. The state of the art in chromatic calorimetry is reviewed, including experimental results from proof-of-concept prototypes and simulation studies investigating quantum-dot-based configurations. Recent progress and current challenges in the development of nanocomposites are also discussed. Finally, future prospects for chromatic calorimetry are outlined.
papers.comment: Contribution to the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP 2026)

papers.title: Quantum control of an electrically levitated nanoparticle with a trapped ion
papers.summary: Quantum control of levitated nanoparticles offers a route towards macroscopic quantum states. Here we propose a novel way to achieve it for a nanoparticle levitated electrically in a linear Paul trap together with a single ion, a system recently realized experimentally. By suitably engineering the trap's AC potential, one can parametrically modulate the ion-nanoparticle distance and thus the Coulomb coupling to enable a resonant interaction. For realistic parameters, we calculate that this enables sympathetic cooling of the nanoparticle to its motional ground state by a single, continuously laser-cooled ion. Additional AC drives enable the preparation of squeezed nanoparticle states and of ion-nanoparticle entanglement. Moreover, non-Gaussian states such as Fock and cat states, prepared in the ion with standard trapped-ion techniques, can be transferred to the nanoparticle with high fidelities. We provide complete protocols for each of these states, including all known decoherence sources. Our results establish electrically trapped ion-nanoparticle systems as a platform for quantum control of levitated matter.

papers.title: Instant-LIVO: Efficient LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry with Compact Geometry and a Bounded Single-Reference-Frame Map
papers.summary: LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry (LIVO) is a fundamental technology for autonomous systems; however, deployment on resource-constrained platforms remains challenging due to physical limitations. This paper presents Instant-LIVO, a tightly coupled, high-speed, real-time LIVO system. The system introduces a compact geometric map based on spatial-hashed OctVox and accelerates local-neighborhood retrieval and plane fitting through cache-assisted heuristic staged K-nearest-neighbor searches. It also employs a bounded single-reference-frame visual map that adaptively updates the reference frame according to the tracking status, while using Schmidt-type uncertainty-aware photometric fusion to maintain the correlation between the reference pose and the current state. The system performs multisensor fusion through a sequential process consisting of IMU prediction, LiDAR geometric correction, and visual photometric correction. It was evaluated on 32 public benchmarks and custom datasets. While maintaining competitive accuracy on both X86 and ARM platforms, Instant-LIVO achieves average processing-speed improvements of approximately 2.3x and 2.1x, respectively, and reduces peak memory usage to approximately 1/20 and 1/13, respectively. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing LIO and LIVO baselines in both accuracy and computational efficiency.The implementation is available at: https://github.com/Faker-0714/Instant-LIVO.git.

papers.title: Navigating Quantum Education at the University level: Pedagogical Pathways and a Roadmap for Textbook Selection
papers.summary: Instruction in quantum mechanics (QM) is often categorized by its entry point as 'wave-first' or 'spin-first', yet these labels lack consistent definitions and overlook other established or emerging approaches. Moreover, while capturing broad differences in topic selection and sequencing, this binary framing obscures critical differences in contextualization--how three dimensions (mathematical tools, phenomena and experiments, and theoretical concepts) are framed and connected to support student sensemaking. Research also rarely examines how such pedagogical choices unfold across the undergraduate-to-graduate trajectory. Using textbooks as an analytical lens to map these choices and characterize overarching pathways, encompassing entry points and overall orientations, we comparatively analyze the selection, sequencing, and contextualization of core topics across these 3 dimensions, alongside prefaces and introductions, in 36 university QM textbooks spanning countries and eras. At the topic level, we show that identical topics occupy widely different curricular roles depending on their contextualization. Synthesizing these findings into pathways, we identify three additional entry-point archetypes (labeled path-, qubit-, and axiom-first) and characterize all 5 approaches, showing that most textbooks combine multiple archetypes in their opening chapters. Extending this synthesis beyond entry points, we map textbooks' overall orientations relative to mathematics, experiment and application, and theoretical physics. Interpreting these profiles alongside authors' rationales reveals how educators navigate competing trade-offs among mathematical accessibility, theoretical generality, physical motivation, and modern developments. This study provides a multidimensional framework, substantive examples, and a practical roadmap for textbook selection and curriculum design in QM education.

papers.title: Nuclear Urca cooling in magnetar crust and anomalous heating
papers.summary: We present a new result that the nuclear Urca process in magnetars, associated with ultrastrong magnetic field, dramatically alters the neutrino cooling efficiency to support higher surface temper ature, which is not common in ordinary neutron stars. A new formalism for neutrino luminosity accommodating finite temperature on top of magnetic field is extended with the use of realistic nuclear structure inputs for the Urca pair 29Na-29Mg. We find that the neutrino luminosity of Urca pair shows a spiral variation as a function of magnetic field and crust density, while the Urca pair persists, in contrast to previous studies. Applying geometrically correct volumetric energy loss rate to Urca shell at fixed density with varying magnetic field strength, our results show that thermally populated excited states at finite temperature enhance neutrino luminosity, whereas conditions con strained Urca-pair formation driven by ultrastrong magnetic field reduce cooling efficiency, which can explain high temperature of magnetar surface as a new possibility.

papers.title: Criterion and Construction Framework for Impure Quantum $(r,δ)$-LRCs from Optimal $(r,δ)$-LRCs
papers.summary: This paper aims to uncover new phenomena and provide new tools for quantum \((r,δ)\)-LRCs derived from optimal \((r,δ)\)-LRCs. The initial motivation is to identify the main reason for the existence of impure cases in such quantum codes. Our main result reveals that whether \(d = r+1\) is the key factor governing the impurity of quantum \((r,δ)\)-LRCs. We prove that, when \(d \neq r+1\), impure quantum codes derived from optimal \((r,δ)\)-LRCs have bounded lengths. Conversely, when \(d = r+1\), we construct impure quantum \((r,δ)\)-LRCs with unbounded lengths. The central tool developed in this work is a criterion for identifying impure quantum codes derived from optimal \((r,δ)\)-LRCs. The main results include a criterion for impurity in quantum \((r,δ)\)-LRCs (Theorem 3.2), a construction framework for impure quantum \((r,δ)\)-LRCs (Theorem 4.4), and two families of impure quantum \((r,δ)\)-LRCs (Theorems 4.8 and 4.11).

papers.title: Manipulation-resistant reputation for peer-to-peer scientific publishing: a combination-therapy approach
papers.summary: In open peer-to-peer networks, where publishing is nearly free and identities are cheap, reputation systems decide what deserves attention, and their metrics become targets for manipulation. We study how to choose and combine reputation signals so that manipulation does not pay while genuine contribution does. Inspired by combination therapies in medicine, we describe each gaming action by its effects on all signals. For aggregation by the minimum of the signals, we prove that, in a global linear model, either some mix of gaming actions raises every signal by more than it costs, or the net gain of gaming is bounded by the imbalance of the attacker's honest profile; locally, gaming brings no first-order gain exactly when an admissible weighting is supported on the attacker's weakest signals. We then specify, without implementing it, MagMell, a two-tier system for peer-to-peer scientific publication: a protocol that orders signed events by Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, enforces budgets and settles staked assessments, and open reputation algorithms that any node can run. Simulations on synthetic data show that minimum aggregation makes networks of fake identities, collusion rings and floods of generated papers lose rank beyond small intensities, at the price of a lower correlation between rank and quality for honest accounts. They also show that criticism is rarely settled, because the evidence needed is seldom available. The replicated log should grow by about 26 kilobytes per identity and year (analytic estimate), and a full recomputation of reputations takes 1.0 to 1.6 seconds for 100,000 identities (measured).

papers.title: Linear and Quadratic Penalties for Cardinality Constraints in Unconstrained Binary Optimization
papers.summary: We study penalty strategies for converting constrained binary optimization problems to quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form on the example of the sparsest $k$-subgraph problem. We adopt an augmented Lagrangian approach involving a linear penalty in addition to the commonly used quadratic one, and show the benefits of this approach. From the constraint structure, we derive sufficient bounds on the penalty coefficients. We conduct extensive experiments comparing combinations of our different penalty strategies with a wide range of classical and quantum QUBO solvers. Our experiments show that to obtain a good-quality solution, the right penalty strategy is almost as important as the quality of the QUBO solver, and iterative approaches appear to be the most efficient. We discuss the mechanisms that lead to a degradation of the solution quality due to large quadratic penalties.

papers.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
papers.summary: There has been significant recent interest in understanding the behaviour of LLM agents from the perspective of human preferences or corpus statistics. In this paper we propose agent states as intermediate variables through which post-training can be measured and predicted. From a statistical physics perspective, we study the emergence of a global potential which governs the transition of state in LLM agent reasoning. We introduce a partition function to model the ideal KL-regularised transition distribution and track potential structure, mean reward and state entropy. We demonstrate our approach in two Qwen3.5-9B tasks: safety-test selection and physics-reasoning auditing. We observe that the potential structure strengthens during post-training as predicted from our framework, while joint changes in reward and state entropy provide consistency evidence. States thus provide a quantitative description of how post-training organises agent behaviour.

papers.title: Do Econophysics-Inspired Inputs Improve Neural Covariance Forecasting? A Leakage-Free Walk-Forward Study of Intraday DJIA Data
papers.summary: Tools from econophysics, including Random Matrix Theory (RMT), Tsallis q-Gaussian tails, Hawkes self-excitation and diffusion-inspired regularization, are often proposed as ingredients for financial risk models, but their incremental value over strong contemporary benchmarks remains unclear. We introduce a Physics-Inspired Neural Covariance (PINC) framework for one-day-ahead covariance forecasting using 1-minute data from the 29 Dow Jones Industrial Average constituents over 545 trading days. The model incorporates RMT-cleaned correlations, Tsallis tail indices and Hawkes intensities as inputs and optionally includes a Fokker-Planck-inspired regularization term selected strictly on validation data. Evaluation is performed through a nested walk-forward design with 11 folds, 231 out-of-sample trading days and multiple random seeds, with explicit leakage controls and reproducibility tests. Neural models outperform static covariance estimators such as sample, Ledoit-Wolf, RMT and EVT-based estimators, but show no statistically significant improvement over HAR-RV or LSTM benchmarks. Validation consistently rejects the physics-inspired regularizer, and ablation studies find no measurable contribution from the RMT, Tsallis or Hawkes features. Portfolio experiments show no statistically significant Sharpe ratio improvement after transaction costs. These results suggest that, for this dataset and forecasting horizon, econophysics-inspired components do not provide measurable benefits beyond strong financial forecasting benchmarks.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables. Empirical study on covariance forecasting, econophysics-inspired machine learning, portfolio optimization, and risk forecasting. Submitted to Results in Physics

papers.title: Geometrical Estimation of Electromagnetic Degrees of Freedom in Reflecting Environments
papers.summary: The number of spatial degrees of freedom (NDoF) of electromagnetic communication channels in reflecting environments is investigated using a full-vector formulation based on dyadic Green's functions and equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents. The channel correlation eigenproblem characterizes the electromagnetic communication modes and their coupling strengths, while the leading-order NDoF is estimated geometrically from the receiver-accessible phase space volume in the electrically large regime. By combining two geometrical projection Jacobians, the phase space volume is related to the mutual shadow area, establishing the equivalence between the two geometrical NDoF formulations and yielding a two-polarization estimate equal to twice the mutual shadow area divided by the squared wavelength. The free-space mutual shadow formulation is extended to perfect electric conductor (PEC) reflecting environments through image construction and phase space ray tracing, accounting for specular reflections and geometrical visibility constraints. The formulation is validated against the eigenvalue spectra of full-vector electromagnetic channels involving planar PEC reflectors, a parabolic reflector, a parallel-plate waveguide, and a non-line-of-sight L-shaped corridor. The geometrical predictions agree with the observed spectral transitions across configurations involving multiple reflections, focusing, and blockage.

papers.title: GAZEAIDE: Recording Gaze Context for Research on AI-Assisted Development
papers.summary: Developers increasingly review code they did not write, much of it generated by AI. Where they look while reading may indicate what is relevant to them, but tools rarely have access to this information. We demonstrate GAZEAIDE, an open-source research prototype for collecting it. Using a webcam, GAZEAIDE estimates which parts of the code a developer looks at and for how long, and records this viewing history together with the text shown on screen. Such context can serve different purposes: providing visual feedback on what has been viewed, guiding code review, and preparing context for a question, which a developer can choose to send to an AI assistant. An IntelliJ plugin records work in the editor; a browser companion records assistant conversations. Attendees can record a short session, replay their viewing history, and try these scenarios.
papers.comment: Submitted to ACM IUI 2027 Demos track

papers.title: The Times They Are A-Changin': Tracking Global Trends through the Lens of Web Search
papers.summary: Human societies have always left traces of their collective priorities, from cave drawings and stone carvings to chronicles on papyrus and printed books. In the digital era, these traces increasingly emerge through social media footprints and web search behavior at a global scale. We construct the first large-scale longitudinal dataset of Google Year in Search trends, spanning 15 years, to characterize how collective public attention evolves across countries and time. Because search engines like Google and Bing do not publicly release raw search logs, Year in Search provides a rare cross-national archive of annually salient search interests. The dataset is supplemented with a manually curated, unified ten-category semantic taxonomy with strong inter-annotator agreement. We focus on four categories (Information Seeking, Personality, Entertainment, and Sports) to investigate how collective attention varies across geographic and socio-cultural contexts. Our analyses reveal a consistently glocalized structure of collective attention: countries converge strongly in profession-level personality attention while remaining differentiated in the specific individuals they search for, yet profession-level similarity is only weakly associated with geographic region and income group. Information seeking is globally dominated by politics and health, while regional distributions show varying degrees of divergence. Crisis periods are associated with both shared and regionally differentiated shifts. Entertainment and sports attention likewise combine globally prominent interests with regional differentiation. Overall, our findings suggest that web search data provide a valuable computational lens for observing collective attention at scale, acting as a living archive of how societal priorities vary across countries and change over time.
papers.comment: This paper has been accepted at the 21st International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM 2027)

papers.title: Analysis of the triply-charm tetraquark states via the QCD sum rules
papers.summary: In this work, we construct the diquark-antidiquark type local currents to interpolate the triply-charm tetraquark states, and investigate the spectroscopy of the scalar, axialvector and tensor triply-charm tetraquark states via the QCD sum rules comprehensively. As a byproduct, we obtain the masses of four vector triply-charm tetraquark states.

papers.title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
papers.summary: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.

papers.title: Quantum-Informed Regularized Poisson Learning for Graph-Based Semi-Supervised Classification
papers.summary: We introduce IPQSSL, a quantum-informed regularized Poisson framework for graph-based semi-supervised classification under scarce labels. Local graph feature contexts are QR factorized, lifted to unitary encodings, and processed by a shared variational circuit whose measurements yield node wise diagonal weights that stabilize a symmetrized Poisson system. We establish positive definiteness of the symmetrized, regularized operator under explicit spectral conditions and derive a Hermitian, block encoding compatible formulation that separates the classical NISQ oriented implementation from a future fault-tolerant pathway. Across seven benchmarks spanning tabular data and a citation network, the effect of regularization is dataset- and budget-dependent: IPQSSL improves over the Poisson baselines on Iris and Wine at all but the single-label budget, reaching 0.946 accuracy on Iris at ten labels per class and at every budget on German Credit, where, however, all methods remain below the majority class rate. Original Poisson remains preferable on Breast Cancer, Heart Disease, Optdigits, and Cora, with the deficit narrowing as the label budget grows on the two largest graphs. Ablations attribute the gains to diagonal stabilization rather than variational training. The result is a resource transparent bridge between Poisson graph learning and quantum linear algebra, with an explicit empirical delineation of when diagonal regularization helps.

papers.title: Effective theory of quantum black holes with Kretschmann scalar
papers.summary: We investigate the thermodynamics, quasinormal modes (QNMs), and shadows of the effective theory of quantum black holes (BHs) by expanding the physical constants in terms of the Kretschmann scalar. The resulting effective metric can contain two horizons, which is typical for a quantum-corrected Schwarzschild spacetime. The second-order corrected metric only shifts the first-order corrected metric, allowing investigation of IR phenomena from the pure first-order corrected one. From a thermodynamic point of view, the metric leads to a stable cold remnant with zero entropy, compatible with the third law of thermodynamics. In the perturbation regime, we use massless scalar perturbations to extract the effective potential, QNMs, graybody factor, and total absorption cross section. We show that double-horizon BHs have a double light ring in the potential, and for a certain value $Ω/χ^2=0.01,$ the QNMs are similar to the GR case since the horizon is Schwarzschild-like. We also tested the correspondence between the QNMs and the graybody factor, and our results still hold with an error far below $1\%$. Our results also conclude that the higher the frequency, the bigger the cross-section area. For the optical observables, we observe that the opposite sign of $Ω$ leads to distinct behavior of the BH's photon sphere and shadow radius. The Sagittarius A* shadow radius upper bound from the Event Horizon Telescope observation in the $2σ$ and $1σ$ significance set the upper limit of the quantum parameter $Ω$ to $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.3649$ and $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.0105$, respectively.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 15 figures, under review in European Physical Journal C

papers.title: Tasklets: A Unit-Test Benchmark for Language Model Architectures
papers.summary: We introduce Tasklets, a benchmark of small synthetic tasks for evaluating the computational capabilities of language model sequence-mixing layers. These tasks probe foundational capabilities such as recall, sequence manipulation, and state tracking. Such tasks are widely used in architecture research, but differences in task selection, formulation, and evaluation make comparisons across studies difficult. Tasklets brings these tasks together, organizing them by the capabilities they test and providing a shared setup for evaluating how different architectural layer types learn fundamental computations. We compare a broad range of layer types through controlled experiments with small models. Our task implementations and evaluation code support reproducible, low-cost testing of new architectural proposals: https://github.com/zaydzuhri/flame/tree/tasklets.

papers.title: Synthesizing Expressive Human-Object Interactions via Test-time Latent Adaptation
papers.summary: When interacting with objects of unknown physical properties, humans sometimes probe, over-exert, stagger, and adjust through iterative adaptation instead of succeeding immediately. We argue that this process is an expressive but largely overlooked aspect of human-object interaction in motion synthesis. Both kinematic data-driven methods and physics-based controllers tend to produce flawlessly executed motions: the former lack sufficient data for learning fine-grained adaptation, while the latter use reinforcement learning (RL) and privileged object dynamics to learn robust, deterministic behaviors. We propose ExpHOI (Expressive Human-Object Interaction), a test-time latent adaptation framework built on an RL-trained physics-based control policy. During policy training, we encode diverse object dynamics contexts into a structured latent space. At test time, Advantage-Weighted Regression (AWR) iteratively optimizes the latent code for an object with unknown physical properties. Temporary mismatches between this code and the true object dynamics produce an expressive progression from tentative, error-prone trials to proficient interaction. Adaptation behaviors inevitably come with occasional failures, so a high-level planner is introduced to handle failed cases to maintain full, consistent animations. We demonstrate our framework's effectiveness on a large-object transportation task, where such adaptation is especially pronounced. To train our framework, we introduce a mass-diverse object dataset with rich physical-property annotations. Across carrying and push-pull, our method pairs over 90% success with markedly higher posture diversity, and is rated the most lifelike in our user study on animation liveliness.

papers.title: Probing grand unification in the dark dimension: proton decay and collider signatures
papers.summary: We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. One-loop four-dimensional MSSM and split-supersymmetric reference running determines electroweak coupling-crossing scales and the residual strong-coupling mismatch. A selected common-threshold benchmark gives a heavy-state mass of $1.137\times10^{16}$ GeV, a reference crossing of $1.139\times10^{16}$ GeV, and a conditional proton partial lifetime of $8.72\times10^{35}$ years. At a micron-scale gravitational length, suppressed baryon-violating matching amplitudes can satisfy proton limits, although the high-scale mass-matching condition selects a distinct region of the scanned geometry. Independently, a $5$ TeV neutral-vector benchmark yields an inclusive leading-order dielectron cross section of $0.183$ fb over $4.5$--$5.5$ TeV at a collider energy of $13.6$ TeV, before detector selection. The analysis provides quantitative effective-model benchmarks and identifies the remaining high-scale matching and experimental tests.

papers.title: Forbidden T-symmetry breaking in time-dependent non-Hermitian systems with gain and loss
papers.summary: Parity-time ($PT$) symmetry has attracted significant interest in photonics and related fields in recent years. With sufficiently weak gain and loss, these systems typically exhibit entirely real energy levels, with all corresponding wave functions remaining $PT$ symmetric. As the strength of gain and loss increases, complex-conjugate energy levels are expected to emerge, signaling the onset of $PT$ symmetry breaking. Similar properties can be found in non-Hermitian systems with other antilinear symmetries as well, where parity is replaced by another operator such as rotation ($R$) or simply the identity operator, resulting in $RT$-symmetric and $T$-symmetric non-Hermitian systems. In this work, we demonstrate that this typical scenario of non-Hermitian symmetry breaking in a finite Hilbert space is forbidden in a class of time-dependent systems with gain and loss and $T$ symmetry: the system remains in its $T$-symmetric phase as we increase the strength of gain and loss, even when the spatial distribution of gain and loss is random. Furthermore, this behavior is also independent of the duration or period of the temporal modulation. In contrast, this forbidden non-Hermitian symmetry breaking does not occur when the same systems are modified to display $PT$ symmetry instead. Our findings highlight contrasting behaviors in time-dependent and time-independent non-Hermitian systems, creating new possibilities and opportunities for future investigations.

papers.title: Saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at LH$μ$C
papers.summary: Motivated by recent proposal of high energy $μ^+$-hadron collider at CERN, LH$μ$C, which could be a natural extension of the LH$e$C at the end of the HL-LHC stage, we have studied expected gluon saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at DIS; these processes are sensitive to the most basic non-perturbative structure parametrizing hadronic content of small-$x$ gluons, the Weizsäcker-Williams (WW) TMD gluon distribution. For the nominal center-of-mass energy of LH$μ$C $\sqrt{s}=5.3$~TeV we have computed a large selection of observables using the ITMD framework in Mote Carlo setting, both for proton and lead target. In the context of future data-driven precise restrictions of the WW TMD gluon distribution, we have computed several azimuthal angle correlations, including the correlations between pairs of jets as well as the outgoing $μ^+$ and jet plane. We have also computed nuclear modification factors, that show a significant suppression, ranging locally between 30%-40%, depending on the observable.

papers.title: Isonomy: Isolating Every Request from Timing Side Channels at Nearly Full-Sharing Throughput in Multi-Instance LLM Prefill
papers.summary: Many long prompts share a prefix, and reusing its cached keys and values saves prefill computation. A cache hit, however, makes the first token arrive earlier and can reveal that another request used the same prefix, so providers share the cache only within an account. Under least privilege, even permission to send and pay for requests should not expose other requests' prompts in the same account. This matters because agents send unreviewed requests carrying private data, resellers pool users behind one account, and creden-tials can be stolen. Isonomy therefore isolates each request by default and lets requests opt into explicit sharing groups. Rather than give up reuse, it keeps one cache shared across accounts and hides only hits on prefixes cached outside a request's group. We target deployments where clients cannot observe one another's load, because there it suffices to hide these hits in the request's own timing. On three commercial APIs, our listeners could not distinguish added prefill work from a short request beyond measurement noise. Built on vLLM, Isonomy's gateway applies the deployment's routing rule to load and visible cache entries only, which yields the instance where the request would run if hidden hits missed. On that instance, the prediction mode estimates when the first token would be ready from the queue and the visible prefix, and gates its release. The execution mode instead reserves the work a hidden hit skips and fills it with other requests' prompts where possible. In direct-probe tests on two, four, and eight instances with every request isolated, both modes kept the upper bound on a probe's advantage within measure-ment noise at both prefix lengths. At saturation, the prediction mode retains 0.98 of unprotected sharing's throughput on two workloads with account labels, whereas isolation by account retains 0.95, or 0.80 where more reuse crosses accounts.

papers.title: Planar Formation Control with Minimal Sensing and No Common Orientation: An Almost-Global Result
papers.summary: Formation control based on geometric constraints often requires either rigid interaction graphs or a common orientation reference. This paper investigates whether a prescribed planar formation can instead be achieved using only $N-1$ pairwise interactions while preserving global rotational freedom. To this end, a guiding-vector-field-inspired framework is developed in which each selected distance relation is represented by a parameterized circular manifold and the remaining geometric freedom is coordinated through relative virtual phases, based on which, a distributed controller is then constructed. The closed-loop system is shown to possess only the desired equilibrium set and a degenerate undesired equilibrium set corresponding to collapse of the central edge. The latter is proved to form a saddle-type equilibrium manifold with a measure-zero stable set, yielding almost-global convergence to the desired formation. In addition, the controller admits an implementation under mutually misaligned local frames using locally expressed relative measurements and scalar phase information.

papers.title: A new restitution model for wet particle collisions using fully resolved numerical simulations
papers.summary: Particle collisions play a central role in wet particle processes such as granulation, drying, and chemical reactors, yet the influence of the liquid on the collision dynamics remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the influence of liquid viscosity, liquid density, liquid content, impact velocity, solid density, and surface tension on the wet restitution coefficient using numerical simulations. In this study, a Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) framework is used that has been validated against dedicated experiments of wet-wet particle collisions, showing a good agreement for both liquid-bridge evolution and rebound dynamics. The restitution coefficient decreases with increasing liquid viscosity, liquid density, and liquid-to-solid density ratio, whereas increasing impact velocity increases rebound. The negligible influence of surface tension indicates that viscous dissipation is the dominant source of energy loss under the investigated conditions. As existing Stokes number formulations were found to only capture part of the governing physics, a generalized Stokes number is proposed to incorporate both the viscous and inertial response time scales. A modified restitution coefficient model based on the generalized Stokes number successfully collapses the numerical and experimental data onto a single trend and predicts the wet restitution coefficient with an RMSE of only 4.99%.
papers.comment: 29 pages, 11 figures, submitted to Chemical Engineering Journal

papers.title: Atomic interferometry based on a phase-jump error signal with suppression of the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift
papers.summary: We develop a method for forming Ramsey fringes in atomic interferometers as a difference error signal using the phase-jump technique for Ramsey pulses (phase-jump error signal). In this case, the measurement procedure can be implemented as stabilization (locking) of the frequency chirp rate at the central zero of the error signal. We show analytically that this approach allows suppressing the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift (LACS). This shift was recently theoretically predicted and experimentally identified in the papers [V. I. Yudin et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{122}, 737 (2025); D. N. Kapusta et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{123}, 388 (2026)]. A characteristic feature of the LACS is an inverse cubic dependence $\propto 1/T^3$ (where $T$ is the time between adjacent Ramsey pulses), and it can become dominant for interferometers with a short baseline. Therefore, the developed measurement algorithm with a phase-jump error signal will enable significant improvement in the metrological performance of compact quantum sensors for various purposes (atomic gravimeters, accelerometers, gyroscopes).

papers.title: The GAPS programme at TNG. LXXXIII. Orbital refinement and atmospheric investigation of TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b)
papers.summary: TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b) is a highly irradiated ultra-hot Jupiter on a strongly misaligned orbit, a benchmark target for atmospheric and dynamical studies. We comprehensively characterise the TOI-1518 system by refining its orbital and physical parameters, and by investigating the chemical composition of the planetary atmosphere through transmission spectroscopy. We employed a joint Bayesian framework combining TESS photometry, HARPS-N high-resolution spectroscopy, and least-squares deconvolution profiles to break stellar geometrical degeneracies. We then applied single-line and cross-correlation function (CCF) transmission spectroscopy across theoretical templates.
